Name: Meghalaya Single Origin Robusta Coffee - 250g
Tasting_Notes: Mild citrus, roasted nuts, cereal, dark chocolate aroma
Desc:
Single-Origin Robusta Meghalaya 
  Redefining Robusta. Bold, rich, and full of character.  
 Most people think of Robusta as harsh or basic. Our  Single-Origin Robusta from Aguragre, Meghalaya  proves otherwise. Sourced directly from a community of over  200+ dedicated farmers , this coffee is hand-picked, naturally sun-dried, and carefully roasted to unlock a flavor experience you won’t expect from Robusta. 
 
 Why This Coffee Stands Out 
 A Unique Origin 
 Grown in the fertile hills of  Aguragre, Meghalaya , this Robusta carries the story of a farming community that has cultivated coffee for generations. Each cup connects you to the people and the land that make it possible. 
 Naturally Processed 
 The beans are  sun-dried under the open sky  and hand-picked at peak ripeness. This traditional method enhances sweetness and complexity while preserving the bean’s natural integrity. 
 Bold Flavor, Elevated Experience 
 Expect  mild citrus brightness balanced with roasted nuts, cereal-like body, and a dark chocolate aroma . Smooth yet robust, it’s a coffee that surprises you with depth and sophistication. 
 Roasted with Care 
 We roast in small batches to bring out the best of this origin—balancing boldness with sweetness so you can enjoy a refined Robusta without bitterness. 
 
 What’s Inside 
 
 
  100% Single-Origin Robusta  
 
 
  Origin:  Aguragre, Meghalaya (200+ farmer community) 
 
 
  Process:  Natural Sun-Dried, Hand-Picked 
 
 
  Roast Levels Available:  Medium Roast / Dark Roast 
 
 
  Flavor Notes:  Mild citrus, roasted nuts, cereal, dark chocolate aroma 
 
 
  Recommended Brewing Methods:  French Press, Moka Pot, Espresso 
 
 
 
 Who Is This For? 
 
 
 Coffee lovers curious to explore  premium Robusta  beyond the ordinary. 
 
 
 Anyone who prefers a  bold, full-bodied cup  that pairs beautifully with milk or stands strong as an espresso. 
 
 
 Adventurous drinkers looking to taste the  hidden gems of Northeast India . 
 
 
 
  Discover Robusta as you’ve never tasted before. From the hills of Meghalaya to your cup—rich, bold, and unforgettable.

Name: Moka Pot Coffee Combo
Desc:
The Ultimate "Wild" Morning Ritual 
 Stop settling for weak coffee. The  Moka Pot Coffee Combo  is curated for those who crave the intensity of an espresso but love the soul of a home-brewed cup. We’ve paired our most powerful bean with the iconic Moka Pot to give you a bold, syrupy brew that cuts through milk and wakes up your senses. 
 Why You Need This Combo 
 
 
  The Perfect Match:  Our Northeast Wild Robusta is high-altitude, high-caffeine, and naturally intense. The Moka Pot is the only brewer designed to handle that level of "wild" and turn it into a smooth, dark-chocolate finish. 
 
 
  Barista Quality, No Machine Needed:  Skip the expensive espresso machine. This combo delivers a heavy-bodied, concentrated brew that serves as the perfect base for Lattes, Cappuccinos, or a killer Iced Americano. 
 
 
  Unbeatable Value:  With  13 to 14 fresh brews  per bag, you’re enjoying premium, single-origin coffee for a fraction of the price of a cafe visit. 
 
 
 
 What’s Inside the Box? 
 
 
  Northeast Wild Robusta (250g):  Experience deep notes of toasted nuts and 85% dark chocolate. 
 
 
  Classic Moka Pot:  The timeless stovetop brewer that extracts maximum flavor and caffeine. 
 
 
 
 Pro Tips for the Perfect Brew 
 To get that "honey-colored" crema and avoid bitterness, follow these quick steps: 
 
 
  Hot Start:  Use pre-heated water in the base to speed up extraction and keep the beans from "cooking" on the stove. 
 
 
  Level, Don't Tamp:  Simply fill the basket and level it off. Let the steam do the work! 
 
 
  The Cold Snap:  As soon as the coffee gurgles and turns pale, remove it from the heat and run the base under cold water. This locks in the sweetness and prevents a burnt taste.

Name: Northeast Cold Brew – Premium Cold Brew Coffee Bags (5 Sachets | 250g )
Tasting_Notes: – What You’ll Experience Gentle fruitiness – Like berries Subtle tamarind tang – Adds bright contrast Cocoa aftertaste
Desc:
Experience the bold, bright taste of the Northeast – in every chilled sip. Cold brew like no other. Smoother. Sweeter. More character. 
   
   
  What Makes Our Cold Brew Unique?  
 Northeast Cold Brew is a medium roast 100% Arabica blend crafted from smallholder farms in Assam, Tripura, and Meghalaya. Designed for cold brew extraction, this blend unlocks an exceptional flavor experience perfect for slow sipping or summer energizing. 
  Blend Details:  
 
 Assam (20%) – Full-bodied depth and richness 
 Tripura (40%) – Balancing brightness and mild acidity 
 Tura, Meghalaya (40%) – Tropical sweetness with gentle fruit layers 
 
   
  Roast Profile:  Medium    Packaging:  5 x ~50g cold brew sachets    Best Brewed Cold:  16 hrs at 4°C | 1:8 ratio for extraction 
   Y ield:  One 50g pouch makes ~500 ml cold brew  
   
  Cold Brew Method (Step-by-Step)  
 
 Tear open a sachet and pour into your brew jar. 
 Add 280–350 ml of cold water (1:8 to 1:10 ratio depending on strength). 
 Steep in the fridge for 16 hours at 4°C. 
 Strain and serve chilled. Optionally add ice or a splash of milk. 
 
  No equipment needed. No bitterness. Just naturally sweet, refreshing coffee with layered flavor complexity.  
   
  Tasting Notes – What You’ll Experience  
 
 Gentle fruitiness – Like berries  
 Subtle tamarind tang – Adds bright contrast 
 Cocoa aftertaste – Rich, smooth finish 
 
   
  A sensory experience that balances acidity, body, and aroma — perfect for iced sipping or slow Sunday mornings.  
   
  Why Choose 7000 Steps Cold Brew?  
 
 Farm-direct Arabica from Northeast India’s finest terroirs 
 No preservatives or additives — 100% pure ground coffee 
 Small-batch roasted for peak flavor retention 
 Easy, mess-free brewing at home 
 
   
   Packaged for freshness in a convenient 250g kit

Roast: Medium Roast The estate is located in the UNESCO World heritage site of Kodagu and forms a part of the elephant corridor.Honey processed coffee is a method where coffee cherries are pulped to remove their outer skin, but the sticky, sugary layer of fruit (called mucilage) is left on the bean while it dries. Because the beans absorb the sugars from the fruit, honey processed coffees features higher sweetness with distinct notes of honey, caramel, or brown sugar. It also has a balanced profile with a creamier, heavier body than washed coffees, but less intense fruitiness than natural coffees and more mellow taste.

Desc: Processing: Naturals, Patio DriedVarietals Grown: Arabica ( Kent)Altitude: 1000 m.a.s.lRoast: Medium RoastFlavour Notes:Flavour Notes: ORANGE CANDY AND BERRIES. An aromatic coffee with balanced, sparkling acidity and a fine body. It is believed that the Kent variety roots back to the first Bourbon seeds brought out of Yemen to India by Baba Budan in 1670. It originates from a selection made by Mr. L.P. Kent in 1911 from a single tree growing in his Doddengooda Estate in Mysore, South Western India. It was widely planted in India since the 1930s and became very well known for its excellent flavour profile. Slowly, due to its susceptibility to many pests and diseases, the Indian farms made a switch to hardier varieties of Arabica and Robusta. Kogilahalla Estate is one among the few estates which has managed to retain its Kent coffee plants. These old plants are specially tended to and a micro lot of ripe fruits are selectively handpicked every year. The berries are then sun dried on raised beds after a short pre-fermentation phase. With its naturally high sugar content, the pre-fermentation step lends the coffee its complex winey notes that complements the syrupy body and enhances aroma. One can easily say that Kent, hands down, is one among the most splendid Indian varieties of Arabica Coffee.

Desc: Origin: Kogilahalla Estate, North CoorgProcessing: Natural SundriedRoast: Medium  RoastVarietals Grown: Arabica (  Kent) Flavour Notes: ORANGE CANDY AND BERRIES. An aromatic coffee with balanced, sparkling acidity and a fine body. It is believed that the Kent variety roots back to the first Bourbon seeds brought out of Yemen to India by Baba Budan in 1670. It originates from a selection made by Mr. L.P. Kent in 1911 from a single tree growing in his Doddengooda Estate in Mysore, South Western India. It was widely planted in India since the 1930s and became very well known for its excellent flavour profile. Slowly, due to its susceptibility to many pests and diseases, the Indian farms made a switch to hardier varieties of Arabica and Robusta.  Kogilahalla Estate is one among the few estates which has managed to retain its Kent coffee plants.  These old plants are specially tended to and a micro lot of ripe fruits are selectively handpicked every year. The berries are then sun dried on raised beds after a short pre-fermentation phase. With its naturally high sugar content, the pre-fermentation step lends the coffee its complex winey notes that complements the syrupy body and enhances aroma. One can easily say that Kent, hands down, is one among the most splendid Indian varieties of Arabica Coffee.

Name: CAFEC Flower Dripper DEEP 27
Desc:

 Inside, the signature flower-shaped ribs create subtle air channels that maintain a steady flow throughout the brew. This prevents clogging and ensures consistency, making it easier to get great results every time. 
 Whether you’re upgrading from simpler brewing methods or refining your daily ritual, the DEEP 27 offers an approachable way to experience specialty coffee at home — with more control, more clarity, and more consistency. 
 It pairs especially well with medium roast Arabica coffees, where notes of cocoa, roasted nuts, and gentle fruit sweetness come through with clarity and depth — without becoming too sharp or too heavy. 
 Finished in a clear brown tone, it reflects a quiet, understated aesthetic — a brewing tool that feels as considered as the coffee you make with it.

Desc:
Our Assorted Drip Coffee Box, a thoughtfully curated collection of single-serve drip coffee sachets for effortless brewing, unique and exceptional flavors. Each box brings together distinctive coffees from different origins, roast profiles, and processing styles - perfect for gifting, or daily indulgence.  Inside, you will find a balanced mix of  - Arabica Medium Roast with smooth, rounded notes - Arabica Dark Roast delivering bold intensity and depth - The iconic Monsooned Malabar, known for its low acidity and earthy richness - Our indulgent Whiskey Barrel Aged Coffee, infused with warm, oaky character - Decaffeinated coffee, offering full-bodied flavor with less caffeine. 
 Each sachet is individually packed to preserve freshness and flavor, allowing you to enjoy coffee anywhere, with no machine required. Whether you’re a seasoned coffee lover or just beginning your journey, this assorted box celebrates variety, craftsmanship, and the joy of discovering something new in every cup.  How to brew?  
 
 Tear open the bag at the top. 
 
 Gently shake to ensure even distribution and place the hanger securely over the cup. 
 Slowly pour hot water into the bag until it reaches the neck. 
 Refill with more water once the filtration process completes. 
 Cease pouring when the brewed coffee level in the cup reaches midway through the filter. 
 Discard the used filter and serve. 
 Brewing time: under 2 minutes. 
 Total hot water required: 200ml.

Desc:

Tasting_Notes: Coffee
Desc:
Coffee Variety -  Arabica Beans   Post Harvest Process   - Washed   Roast level   - Medium Roast    Region   - Mudigere, Chikmagalur    Kolli Berri Estate in Mudigere, 30 km from Chikmagalur, a women-led enterprise run by Pranathi Shetty. The cup is clean, uniform, and marked by bold flavors that cut through with clarity and balance. Designed for everyday drinking, it carries both strength and refinement - dependable yet distinctive.  
  The coffee starts with a comforting malt-like aroma. In the cup, notes of dark chocolate take center stage, followed by hints of ripe prunes that add depth and sweetness. A gentle acidity brings brightness, while the rounded body creates a smooth and satisfying mouthfeel. Clean and well-structured, the cup showcases consistency from start to finish, ending with delicate traces of cocoa and dried fruit.  
  The coffee cherries were harvested at peak ripeness from farms located between 3,500 and 3,750 feet above sea level. After harvest, the cherries were carefully sorted, with all floaters and defective fruit removed before pulping. The parchment coffee was then fermented to break down the remaining mucilage, washed thoroughly, and slowly dried. This careful washed process helps preserve the coffee's sweetness, clarity, and uniform character in the final cup.

Coffee Variety -  Chandragiri Arabica Beans   Post Harvest Process   - Wild Fig Co-Ferment, Washed Arabica   Roast level   - Medium Roast    Region   -  Kalledevarapura Estate, Bababudangiri, Chikmagalur   Some ideas begin not in the lab or the market — but underfoot. 
 This micro-lot was born not out of invention, but observation. One morning walk, somewhere between the canopy and the soil, a whisper of possibility stirred. Wild figs - soft, fallen, sticky-sweet, scattered the forest floor like little forgotten gifts. Not harvested. Not sold. Just there. Fermenting into the earth. 
 In that moment, something shifted. What if the forest had already done half the work? What if nature, in her quiet generosity, had left behind an ingredient that was both abundant and invisible, until you slowed down enough to see it?

Name: Anaerobic Naturals
Tasting_Notes: Ripe Jackfruit BREW
Desc:
Coffee   
  Arabica Anaerobic Naturals  
 During this year's harvest, our team worked closely with two producer families to produce this surprising coffee. We carried out an extended fermentation over a period of 96 hours in closed, anaerobic conditions of coffee fruit, and the result is a jammy jackfruit flavour profile! 
  FLAVOUR NOTES:  Ripe Jackfruit 
  BREW:  Pour Over 
  RECIPE:  For a pour over, place a filter in your dripper and rinse with hot water to eliminate the taste of paper. Add 15g of medium-ground coffee. Pour 250ml of hot water (92-94°C) in slow, circular motions, starting from the centre and moving outward, allowing the coffee to bloom, and continue pouring until the desired amount of water has passed through. 
  NOTE:  The 'best brewed with' list suggests methods for the best cup, but isn’t restrictive—this coffee can be ground and brewed however you prefer. 
   
 
 
 Meet the Grower 
 
  ORIGIN:  BR Hills, Karnataka 
  GROWER:  Madevi, Madammma, Basavanna and Madegowda 
  ABOUT:  In a remote hamlet nestled deep within the BR Hills Tiger Reserve, family members and neighbours—our partner producers—took a bold risk with this coffee. They watched with equal parts patience and nervousness as freshly picked coffee cherries turned from bright red to deep purple, slowly fermenting without air. Their young children and a mischievous baby goat named Ganesha offered a welcome distraction during those tense, uncertain days. 
  PRICE PAID IN 2025:  
  Rs 1000/kg ~ $11.8/kg for equivalent green coffee  
  2.4x the Fair Trade minimum price  
 Our price isn’t driven by speculative markets but reflects quality and the growers' commitment to biodiversity-friendly farming. Our higher price floor ensures a more sustainable income for farmers.   
  Our 2025 Microlots   
 The 2025 harvest has been our most experimental yet, with over 12 small, experimental lots dropping every month. This season, 21 of our partner producers worked with Asjad Ahmed and Arshiya Bose (both Q-Post-Harvest Professionals) to craft some deeply flavourful and fun Arabicas.  
  WHY:  But beyond taste, the Microlot Programme is a vital part of our mission to strengthen smallholder livelihoods. Through this programme, producers can earn over 1.4x the market price, helping them break cycles of debt. The impact goes beyond income—one of our producers shared how producing yellow honey coffee allows her to hold on to her harvest, preventing a family member from selling it off at a fraction of its value just to fund his next drink. 
  JOIN US:  These microlots are more than coffee; they’re about resilience, dignity, and meaningful change.

Name: Cascara
Desc:
Know the Cascara 
 
 
  Cascara tastes nothing like coffee! The word, Cascara which can be translated from Spanish to mean "husk", is an increasingly popular byproduct of coffee processing. After coffee fruit is picked and pulped, the fruity pulp is dried to produce cascara, also known as dried coffee cherries. Our version is slightly tweaked, it is cascara in its original form, the husk of fruit after both have been dried together. Cascara can be brewed like loose leaf tea, steeped in hot water or as a cold brew. Although it does contain caffeine, it is about a quarter of that of coffee and jampacked with antioxidants. We love coffee but we're nudging you to try a lesser known part of coffee's journey!  
 
 
   
 
 
 Know the Grower 
 
 
 
 
 The Arabica from which this Cascara comes, has been grown by our  partner producers in Biligirirangan Hills. This region, BRT as it is fondly known is a magnificent forest with elevational gradients that go from 800 to 1600m! This unique range in altitude enables all major forest types and this in turn produces a magical cup of coffee...and cascara!  
 How to Use 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 You can enjoy both hot and cold brew versions. Here is our recommended recipe: 
 Cascara Tonic: 
 
 
 
  Ingredients: 1 tbsp C  ascara   3 cups Water 2 tbsp Jaggery Tonic Water Lime Ice  
  Method: Simmer the Cascara, water and jaggery on medium heat for about 10-15 minutes till the volume is reduced to half. Allow it to cool, strain the mixture, and refrigerate. To make the Cascara Tonic, add ice cubes into a tall glass, pour 90 ml of the Cascara brew, the juice of half a lime and top with tonic water. Garnish with a slice of lime.  
  Developed in partnership with The Locavore & Chef Thomas Zacharias

Name: Chukki
Tasting_Notes: of dark chocolate
Desc:
Meet the Coffee 
 
     
 This coffee is a Vienna Roast, dry ferment of carefully picked, sorted, pulped and washed Arabica. It was dry fermented in a barrel with pulped Arabica for 36 hours. While roasting, we particularly extended our development time on this one. The result is a brew with tasting notes of dark chocolate, roasted almonds and lingering caramel. This is best brewed with an Aeropress and Moka pot. Enjoy it black or with milk!  
 
 
 Meet the Grower 
 
 
 
 
    This beautiful Arabica coffee comes from our partner producers in the Biligirirangan Hills of Karnataka. This collective of growers is dreaming big about the wellbeing of their community and we are equally committed to enabling them to find their way. BR Hills is a magnificent forested landscape with elevational gradients that go from 800 to 1600m! This unique range in altitude enables all major forest types and this in turn produces a magical cup of coffee!    
 Who's Chukki? 
 
 
 
 Kethegowda decided where to set the camera trap - at the perimeter his coffee farm shares with the forest. She’s not the first Leopard we’ve spotted, but certainly is one that takes delight in making repeated visits to Kethegowda’s farm. The camera has been able to spot and capture her least once every month since the set-up. After a short, but happening discussion we decided to name her Chukki. Thanks to their cautious and elusive behaviour, we are yet to encounter one in daylight, despite sharing the neighbourhood. They’re usually active and preying at night. Being an apex predator makes the Leopard an indispensable part of the food chain and ecological balance of the region and the planet. Their continuous survival requires an abundance of prey and forest cover. Their population is mostly threatened by habitat loss from forest fragmentation. This gives us more reason to remain committed to growing coffee in the way that we do - under the canopy of native, moist deciduous forest trees and not despite it! Environment conditions that allow these leopards to thrive are the ones that make possible the production of coffee too. We’d like to declare that the Panthera Pardus is a partner producer on this one.

Name: Coffee Canister
Desc:
Know the Artist

 Know Enamel 
 
 
 
 This coffee canister is made of stainless steel, which has then been subjected to the ancient process of enamelling. It’s interesting to note that enamelling dates as far back as the Mesopotamian civilisation and was a technique developed for jewellery! 
 Our previously much-loved canisters deserved a second edition! This one is slightly bigger than the original green canister and can hold little over 600g whole bean. These are  not  microwave or dishwasher-safe. Although this canister is sturdy and it will not shatter into pieces if dropped, it will show small cracks in the enamel coat from repeated damage. Heavy duty so your cute+aggressive pets cannot destroy, safe to store their treats in it! 
   These are handmade, each enamel canister is slightly different.

Name: Handloom Pour Over Filters
Tasting_Notes: Cloth filters produce a clean, sediment-free cup of coffee with heavy aromatics and a buttery mouthfeel from natural
Desc:
Why Handlooom, Not Paper! 
 
  These handloom coffee filters are made from kora (unbleached & undyed) cotton yarn of 60’s x 40’s count. Cloth filters produce a clean, sediment-free cup of coffee with heavy aromatics and a buttery mouthfeel from natural oils and a higher perceived acidity in the brew. Once used, the cloth filter must be washed thoroughly with water only and left to air dry. We have used each cloth filter for over a hundred times before repurposing. In comparison, paper filters are more tightly woven, clean out most sediments and natural oils so your cup of coffee is clean but diminished in aromatic oils. They are also not reusable and as a result, high waste (both in terms of household waste as well in the use of trees at the paper mill).   
 
 
   
 
 
 Fabrics of Resilience 
 
 
 
 These handloom coffee filters celebrate local community and resilience in a time of crisis. The fabric that makes up these filters comes from the award winning organisation, Dastkar Andhra who have been working to revive handloom weaving in the villages of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh for many decades. The stitching of the cloth filters is done by the mothers of the children who are a part of an also award-winning organisation, Parikrma Humanity Foundation in Bangalore. Many parents are small-scale tailors who have faced significant hardships as a result of the recent pandemic. Retailing 30 sets of coffee filters a month allows us to support an entire household.   The cloth filters are a part of Parikrma's community development programme for parents whose livelihoods have been affected by the recent pandemic. 
 How to Use 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Cloth filters can be washed and reused multiple times (but not for eternity!). To get the best use from them, first rinse a few times with hot water before you begin to brew. Once you are done, you can rinse again with hot water and hang to air dry. Do not wring or squeeze dry as it might change the shape. These filters may shrink in size over time, we have tried to factor this in but each filter is an individual too! You will need to adjust and experiment with your grind size, brewing time and perhaps even ratio to get the best brew out of these cloth filters.   If it helps for us to be truthful, we only use cloth filters these days and have been for the past two years almost. We are happy with our brews and would never consider going back to paper.

Name: Lactic Process
Tasting_Notes: Molasses, Clove & Dried Fruit
Desc:
Meet the Producers of Lactic Wash  
  We are continuously inspired by our partner producers – especially those who choose to take fermentation risks with us! We want to acknowledge the courage it takes to try out a new coffee processing technique. In most cases, the producers of our Microlots, like this Lactic Process, are the first people in their hamlets to have ever tried out these methods and we can't wait for you to try it! Let us know what you think and we'll pass on your feedback.  
  Producers: Madegowda, Masthegowda & Basamma, BR Hills  
 
  You've tried      Lactobacillus      in curd but have you in coffee?  
 
  This diverse group of bacteria is abundant in nature, inside our bodies and in our food. In post-harvest processing of coffee, sugary coffee fruits are kept in anaerobic conditions such that the LAB bacteria can eat away at all the sugars. This fermentation produces metabolites that are then absorbed by the coffee beans to produce flavour.  
  Many microorganisms ferment coffee fruit, but through close monitoring of pH, temperature and oxygen availability, we can create environmental conditions that preferentially allow LAB to thrive.   
  Carrying out controlled fermentations is complex - there are many variables to account for and there is no set recipe for a lactic process coffee. Pushing a lactic fermentation can result in overly bitter cups whereas if you get it right, your brew could be buttery, fruity and floral.  
  This was our first collective attempt at a Lactic Process. Full disclosure, we're happy-ish and think that we perhaps need to modify the fermentation time for future experiments.  
  The coffee is delicious, despite all challenges, and we're very happy to be sharing it with you!  
  Flavour Notes:  
 Molasses, Clove & Dried Fruit 
  Recommended Brewing:  
 Pourover & Drip Filter 
  AeroPress : Use a Medium or Medium Coarse Grind, 1:15 ratio and start with 15g, use 2 paper filters or 1 of our cloth filters.

Name: Lappet Moth – Lapel Pin
Desc:
Know the Artist 
 The artist, Kalabati Majumdar has created thoughtful depictions of the interconnectedness between coffee producers, coffee farms and the ecosystem. These enamel coffee mugs are our first foray into the world of 'merchandise' but perhaps more importantly, a daily reminder we need to be mindful of our footsteps and footprints on the natural world...and that change is possible, one cup at a time. 
 
 
   
 
 
 Know Enamel 
 
 
 
 This enamel coffee mug is crafted from solid iron and then carefully coated with enamel. An intriguing historical fact is that enameling traces its origins back to the Mesopotamian civilization, originally developed for jewelry making! 
 The mug can hold approximately 350 ml, and is  not  microwave or dishwasher-safe. While robust and resistant to shattering upon impact, repeated damage may result in minor cracks on the enamel coating. 
   Each mug is handmade, imbuing it with a unique character, so each mug could be slightly different in appearance.

Name: Microlot 36 | Anaerobic Fermentation of Washed Arabica
Desc:
Monthly Microlots   
 
 We do Microlots because Indian coffee is simply far too diverse and heterogenous to standardise flavour profiles from coffee beans, especially where the, geographical, sociocultural and ecological life histories of these coffees is so different. Since we work directly with so many smallholder producers, we end up with many beautiful but very small, experimental lots of coffee. Find them here! 
 
 Microlot 36 | Anaerobic Fermentation of   Washed Arabica 
 
 For Microlot 36, we chose to work with washed Arabica. A very special and small lot is anaerobically fermented in Maadhegowda’s farm in the deciduous forests of BR Hills, at the confluence of the eastern and western ghats. We must mention and expand on the microclimate at play, because it’s critical in allowing and influencing the diversity of microbes that can exist - in that controlled environment within a container in the absence of oxygen.  
 Post the fermentation stage, untimely rains or the lack of them dictate the length of coffee drying periods as well as the amount of care and scrutiny required. No clear distinction in seasons, as years pass by, is also a factor and cause of uncertainty. We dried these fermented and washed beans for 10-11 days. Post two months of green beans resting, we roasted them light medium.  
 The flavour profile: Peach-like sweet acidity, light hibiscus with a strong aroma. Earl grey tea-like body and finish. 
   
  Recommended Brewing:   
 This one is best brewed with an Aeropress and Pour over. It works surprisingly well on a French press too!

 Ever imagined living and farming amidst the wild? Well, with ‘development’ creeping into natural spaces, an elephant in your backyard might not be too far from reality soon. As human and animal habitats intertwine, finding innovative ways to coexist has never been more urgent.   Our speakers for the day have been working together on the ground since 2016, paving the way for harmony between humans and animals through thoughtful collaboration. Join us as  Anandram Reddy , a millet-and-mango farmer living adjacent to the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu, and  Nishant Srinivasaiah , a behavioural ecologist, take us through their experiences of innovating practical ways to address human-elephant conflict, reduce crop losses and improve farmer livelihoods!

Name: The Ant Loop Set
Desc:
The Ant Loop Gift Box 
   
 
 A stunning gift box for ant lovers, someone discovering coffee...or just a collector of one-of-a-kind brewing equipment! 
 
   
 
 Our pitch is for gifts that are kinder to the planet! This gift box has no plastic packaging, is beautifully presented and designed for both somebody discovering coffee and for someone who appreciates traditional craftsmanship in their coffee brewing equipment.  The brass filter coffee is a uniquely South Asian coffee brewing technique which involves a fairly slow percolation of finely ground coffee in a traditional filter. The result is a heavy bodied and rich brew that is delicious both hot or as an iced version. 
   
 
  Gift Sustainably: If you'd like to customise gift boxes with bulk discounts, please fill out this form below and someone from our team will reach out to you: 
   
  Inquiry for Sustainable Gifting  
 
 
 
 
 Why Ants? 
 
 
 
 
    Because, to grow good coffee, one needs ants!  
 
Ants are remarkable indicators of ecological health in coffee farms because they play essential roles in pest control, soil aeration, and nutrient cycling. Their presence often signals a balanced ecosystem, as they keep pest populations in check and contribute to the soil's richness. By studying ant diversity, we get insights into the farm’s overall biodiversity, showing how interconnected and resilient the environment truly is. Plus, they're funny, cute little creatures with fascinating social structures, making them fab mascots for sustainable farming! 
   
 
   Here’s an ode to ants: our coffee companions all the way from farms right up to our kitchen counters! 
 
 
   
 
 
 The Contents 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  Ant Loop Gift Box:   - 100g of coffee of your choice* - Ant Loop Brass Filter - Ant Loop Brass Tumbler Set 
 
  *If you forget to mention this, we'll send you our Whistling Schoolboy coffee. This coffee is only available as a Medium Fine grind. If you would like Whole Bean, select a different coffee! 
   
 
    Optional Add-Ons:   - Brass Tumbler Set - Wooden Ant Scoop  - Ant Tote Bag - Ceramic Ant Pour Over - Ceramic Ant Mug - 100g of Dark Jaggery 
 
   
 
 
 About the Artist 
  Rajiv Eipe makes picture books, comics and short animation films. He has been known to maintain an untidy desk, doodle in sketchbooks, drink too much coffee, and stare into vacant space when confronted with difficult deadlines.

  We along with so many others have swooned for two seasons over the incredible Yellow Honey that Pavan produces every year. This year, the team at the Venkids Valley Estate decided to take their Catuai a step further, from a Yellow Honey process to a Red Honey process and take our word for it, this is an exceptional coffee. Name: Pulney Coffee (Washed) - Pulney Hills - Medium Roast
Tasting_Notes: Citrus Fruits, Cherries, and Nuts
Desc:
Farm: Laks Farm, Pachalur Village 
 Planter: Mr. H.R. Iyer 
 Elevation: 4920 ft. 
 Variety: Chandragiri and SL9 
 Processing: Washed 
 Roast: Medium 
 Tasting notes: Citrus Fruits, Cherries, and Nuts 
 Originating from one of the highest growing regions in Tamil Nadu, these coffees are dense and have a beautiful aftertaste because of the high growing Region. The Laks farm is completely organic and devoid of any chemical pesticides and fertilisers. The coffees are intercropped with oranges, cardamom, pepper and banana. The beans of the highest brix are identified (colour coded bands are given to workers at the estate to pick the cherries). They are sorted for defects twice before using the penagos washer + pulper. Floats are removed and the coffee beans with little bit of mucilage are dried on raised beds. They are exposed to the morning sun for the first two days and then completely dried in shade for a period of 20-25 days. 
 Mr. Iyer is without doubt one of the sweetest and most earnest people we have encountered in coffee and with passion and efforts of Viggnesh in processing, this coffee was one of the best washed coffees we tasted this year! This medium roast has sweet notes of Cherry, and Nuts with a mild Citrus Acidity, and works really well both black and with milk, as a filter or an an espresso!

Name: Venkids Valley Estate (Washed) – Coorg - Medium Dark Roast
Tasting_Notes: Mexican chocolate, Caramel, and Orange Zest A short, scenic drive from Madikeri, past a rivulet or two
Desc:
Elevation: 3600 ft. 
 Varietal: SLN6 
 Processing: Washed 
 Roast: Medium 
 Tasting notes: Mexican chocolate, Caramel, and Orange Zest 
 A short, scenic drive from Madikeri, past a rivulet or two, leads you to the charming “Papakuchi Coffee” by Venkids Valley Estate, where you are welcomed by Pavan and his wife Shilpa. The estate spreads across 200 acres, and is divided into “Patte” or fields, named aptly by the workers. Imagine being able to spot the exact patch of land your coffee was grown on. Yes, that’s the level of traceability Pavan is able to achieve at this estate. 
 This SLN6, grown in the “Kenjipatte” is roasted to slightly darker than a medium (some might even call it a medium) to really enhance the syrupy body and the notes of caramel which are offset by the a splash of orange zest. Pretty great for filters, great for espresso! 
 Pick you grind and brew away!

Name: Vin Van Gogh - Medium Roast
Tasting_Notes: Berries, almonds, and spiced Chocolate The
Desc:
Elevation: 3200-4250 ft. 
 Varietal: SL6, Sln9, Sln5B 
 Planters: Pavan Najappa and Navin Rajes 
 Processing: Washed 
 Roast: Medium dark 
 Tasting notes: Berries, almonds, and spiced Chocolate 
 The origin of this blend goes a fair way back to when Pavan (Venkids Valley Estate) and Navin (Moganad Estate) were schoolmates and were busy making plans for the world domination of Indian speciality coffee! Little did they know then, that the catalyst for this would be small roastery out of Chandigarh, of all the places who would put their two phenomenal washed arabicas together in a top secret ratio, name it after the one of the greatest painters of all time, which is also a word play on their names, and make it the most the delicious, versatile blend to have ever come out of the greater Chandigarh region! Pavan and Navin still remain very tight, and share flights, coffees, jokes, and the roasters they choose to work with! Thankfully, they both agreed to partner with us, which in turn enabled us to come up with this super tasty, bright like a Red Vineyard, over The Cafe Terrace at night, lit up by The Starry Night 
 All stories aside our Vin Van Gogh is our answer to a coffee blend that does everything very very well! It makes a great fruity filter coffee, as well the perfect espresso to have as it is, or a lovely fluffy cappuccino! Pick the grind of your choice, and bask in the glory of Vin’s and Van’s artistry!

Desc:

 Planters: Navin Rajes, and Pavan Nanjappa 
 Processing: Washed Arabica and Naturals Robusta 
 Roast: Medium Dark 
 This blend features the lovely washed arabica from the Moganad Estate, and the natural processed robusta from the Venkids Valley Estate. But beware, if you’re expecting a bitter, boring blend, this will let you down! Ro-Busta Rhymes is a super duper tasty blend that really brings the best out both species of the coffees, but what’s really interesting is that acidity and the sweetness in this blend comes a great deal from the Robusta! We recommend you try this blend black just to really get a feel of what the robusta brings to it!

Name: Satchmo - Dark Roast
Tasting_Notes: Chocolate, Dark Caramel, and hints of Citrus Chocolate, Dark Caramel and hints of citrus
Desc:
Elevation: 3200-3400 ft. 
 Varietal: SL6 & SL9 
 Planters: Pavan Nanjappa & Sharan Gowda 
 Processing: Washed 
 Roast: Medium Dark 
 Tasting notes: Chocolate, Dark Caramel, and hints of Citrus 
 Chocolate, Dark Caramel and hints of citrus, sounds to us like one of the magnificent trumpet solos of the one the only Louis Armstrong! For us, Louis Armstrong a.k.a. Satchmo is the epitome of balance, with a voice that can go from a deep, rich gravel to almost fragile falsettos. Every moment of every song is filled with gorgeous melody, depth and genius improvisations! 
 “Satchmo” the blend, just like it’s muse, has pitch perfect sweetness, a deep body that swells like a crescendo, and a subtle “Vibratoesque” citrus acidity. A coffee that goes not toe to toe, but “Cheek to Cheek” with all accompaniments. The blend is on the darker side of a medium, and has the richness of chocolate and dark caramel, and a raspy acidity that can cut through whatever you throw at it, yes we’re looking at you milk and sugar. Satchmo makes the perfect espressos, moka pots, french presses, south indian filters, and what not, to get you a coffee that’ll make you see sit across and think “What a Wonderful World”

 Meera - A fearless espresso blend that breaks the conventions of what an espresso blend should be! Meera is our Medium-light roast espresso blend with notes of strawberries, baker’s chocolate, vanilla and decadent caramel. What do we get when we blend a clean bright washed and a super sweet, jammy Natural Naturals? A yummy, sweet, super complex, rich espresso, which holds its own in milk beverages as well!

  Dose : Being a lighter roast, we would recommend dosing one-half a gram lesser than what you would dose for a medium/medium dark roast coffee 
  Grind Size:  Grind a step or two finer than what you would normally for a medium roast 
  Yield:  We recommend a yield of 2.5 times the dose of the dry coffee. For eg: Dose: 20 grams; Yield: 50 grams 
  Time:  The lighter the roast, the more you need to extract to get good sweetness and complexity. We like shots between 28-33 seconds for a straight 9-bar approach for Meera. If you can pressure profile, we like to start with a 5-second pre-infusion at 2 bars, and then ramp up to 8 bars till we hit the desired yield, which usually takes around 45-50 seconds.

Make sure, you dose correctly and evenly, WDT is highly recommended here, tamp as evenly as you can and clean around the edges of the portafilter. This will minimise channelling and give you a more even extraction.

Desc:

  Roast: Light  
  Producers: Hoysala Coffee

  The Hoysala Estate was started in the late 1800s is has been family-owned since the 1950's. This washed process lot comes from their farm located in Angadi village near Chikmagalur where the Hoysala Dynasty started in the 9th century. Sunil & Mohan and their families have taken Hoysala coffee to similar heights through their incredible knowledge and expertise in growing, and processing coffee. Working with them for the first time during this harvest, and trying some of their coffees really blew us away.  
  Like other coffees at their farm, this washed coffee is grown using regenerative farming practices, and no chemical fertilisers. This fermented-washed Sachimore was one of our favourite washed coffees from the previous year's harvest and features a delicate floral note reminiscent of coffee blossom. With a medium-light roast, the coffee has developed a lovely stone fruit sweetness and a subtle orange acidity.  
  This coffee works superbly as a filter and as an espresso, and pairs very well with small milk beverages like a cortado or macchiato. We hope you love this one as much as we have!

Tasting_Notes: Amla, Kinnow & Jaggery As many of you might know, Sharan was one of the first
Desc:
Elevation: 1100 MASL  
  Variety: S795  
  Processing: Red Honey  
  Fermentation: 72 hours Anaerobic fermentation  
  Roast: Light  
  Producers: Sharan Gowda  
    Tasting notes: Amla, Kinnow & Jaggery  
 As many of you might know, Sharan was one of the first farmers we ever bought coffee from, in fact he was the first planter we ever met in real life! Back then Salawara Estate was just starting their speciality coffee journey, but in the last five years, they have undoubtedly emerged as one of the most outstanding coffee producers in the country. Their steadfast focus on agriculture and improving their infrastructure rather than content creation has yielded incredible results, and we're the ones reaping the benefits! 
 This year we purchased four lots from them, but this Anaerobic Red Honey was by far our favourite when we cupped it, and with the final roast profile, it's one of the juiciest coffees we have tasted in a while! This S795 grown at 1100 MASL was the last batch of coffee that was processed last year, and the slow maturation, with a higher mucilage content made this the perfect bunch for an Anerobic Red Honey Process. The Cherries were pulped lightly, leaving a lot of the mucilage and were then fermented Anaerobically for 72 hours before they were slow dried for 22 days. The cherries and the process produced a very fruit forward cup, high in sweetness and acidity. 
 To accentuate this, we roasted this super light, and the result is a super juicy coffee with notes of Blackberries, Orange Zest and a lingering sugarcane sweetness.

Name: Elkhill Estates
Tasting_Notes: Our debut coffee from Elkhill, a group of
Desc:
Our debut coffee from Elkhill, a group of estates spanning 1500 acres, this anaerobic washed lot comes from their first year of specialty cultivation. It brews balanced cups with layers of fruit and spice, and a subtle hint of nuts. 
 Ripe cherries, harvested at elevations between 457 to 1067 MASL, were fermented for 36 hours. Next, they were washed then slow-dried on raised beds for nearly 18 days to preserve their character.    
 Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that opens with the aroma of brown sugar and roasted almonds. Each sip is reminiscent of orange, brown spice, and roasted hazelnut, and ends in a lingering, orange zest-like finish. 
 Our roasters recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, a cold brew, or using a Moka Pot. It tastes great black and also works well with milk. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    11  Days  
   
 Note:   This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Araku - Viishalakshi FPC
Desc:
Every harvest brings the excitement of new partnerships and new coffees. This season, we’re proud to introduce our debut lot from Viishalakshi Farmer Producer Company (FPC) in Araku Valley. Named after the valley’s wide-eyed goddess, the FPC brings together 33  tribal villages around Kusumaguda. This lot comes from seven of those villages, where coffee cultivation is led by women and processed at a communal facility.  
 Rooted in natural farming practices for generations, the farmers use composted fruit and vegetable waste to nourish the soil and neem oil treatments to safeguard against pests. Formed last year, Vishalakshi has helped guide these villages from commercial coffee cultivation towards specialty practices. There is now a growing focus on pruning plants, selective picking, proper storage of beans, and careful processing.   
 Roasted to a medium profile, this honey sun-dried lot brews clean, balanced cups. It opens with brown sugar and melon, giving way to roasted almonds, prunes, and a whisper of brown spice. The body is round and syrupy; the finish is long and zesty.   
  We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or using a French Press or Channi.  It tastes great black as well as with milk. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    11  Days  
 
  Note:    This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Raxidi Lobo Estate - Anaerobic Natural
Tasting_Notes: We've been excited to collaborate with Raxidi Lobo
Desc:
We've been excited to collaborate with Raxidi Lobo Estate since their debut with us last year. So, when we first tasted a sample of this anaerobic natural lot, we knew it had to be a part of  Harvest '26 .   
 To bring it to life, the producers started fermenting some of the season's best cherries.  Introducing a specially curated yeast strain to the mix, they let the process go on for 48 hours. Finally, slow drying on raised beds for 21 days locked flavour.   
 Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that carries the sweet nostalgia of drinking mosambi juice in summer. It opens with berries and cherry on the nose, then settles into tart-sweet, bright notes of mosambi, green apple, and plum. The mouthfeel is velvety with a medium body, and the finish is long and tea-like.   
 Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress. 
 
  Recommended Resting Period:    11  Days  
 
  Note:    This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Kerehaklu Estate
Tasting_Notes: Harvest '26 debuts with a bright, citrusy light
Desc:
Harvest '26 debuts with a bright, citrusy light roast.  A Kerehaklu special, it shows Pranoy and Ajoy's sure hand with washed processing.  
 Ripe red Selection 9 cherries collected by seasoned pickers marked the lot's foundation. The producers then used a starter made from the farm's local microbes to aid fermentation. Monitoring temperature and pH regularly, they finished within 37 hours. Next, the coffee was mechanically washed and dried in the shade for three days. Finally, 12 days of polyhouse drying on raised beds locked its flavour. This controlled, aerobic washed process built complexity while harnessing the bean's inherent character.   
 Roasted to a light profile, the coffee delivers clean cups that open with the aroma of orange blossoms and brown sugar. Notes of orange, black tea, and green grapes follow, wrapped in a juicy mouthfeel. Expect low bitterness, medium-high acidity, and a lingering finish of orange marmalade.   
 Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress. 
  Recommended Resting Period:     12 Days  
     Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Half - Caff
Tasting_Notes: Our first-ever single
Process: coffee to create a complex and distinctive cup
Desc:
Our first-ever single-origin, specialty Half-Caff comes from Yelnoorkhan Estate. We selected their S795, washed processed coffee to create a complex and distinctive cup.   
 To reduce caffeine by 55%, we used CO₂ decaffeination, a chemical-free, minimal-waste generating method that is conscious in its water and energy usage. We chose it because the other decaffeination methods available to us in India came with a catch. In removing all the caffeine, they also took away the depth that makes a cup memorable. Adding artificial flavours was not something we wanted to do, never mind the fact that many of these methods also used far too much water.   
 The result is a cup with a gentler kick that holds its own in terms of flavour. You’ll first notice chocolate biscuits on the nose as well as your palate. A silky mouthfeel then reveals notes of roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish.  
 For the best experience, brew this coffee using an espresso machine. It tastes great black and is equally suited to milk-based beverages. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    5    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

 To reduce caffeine by 55%, we used CO₂ decaffeination, a chemical-free, minimal-waste generating method that is conscious in its water and energy usage. We chose it because the other decaffeination methods available to us in India came with a catch. In removing all the caffeine, they also took away the depth that makes a cup memorable. Adding artificial flavours was not something we wanted to do, never mind the fact that many of these methods also used far too much water.   
 The result is a cup with a gentler kick that holds its own in terms of flavour. You’ll first notice chocolate biscuits on the nose as well as your palate. A silky mouthfeel then reveals notes of roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish.  
 For the best experience, brew this coffee using an espresso machine. It tastes great black and is equally suited to milk-based beverages. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    5    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Monsoon Malabar AA- Hoysala Estate
Tasting_Notes: We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala
Desc:
We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala Estate. The unique flavour profile of this coffee develops when winds and humidity from seasonal monsoon rain change the characteristics of the  coffee beans . While this process has its accidental roots in colonial India when a shipment to Europe was attacked by the full force of monsoon winds, similar conditions have been recreated in a controlled environment for consistency in every lot produced.  
 When roasted medium-dark, the result is a medium-bodied cup that invites with sweet aromas of butter biscuits, treating you to notes of  cocoa nib s and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate. Best enjoyed when brewed as an espresso, in the Moka Pot or the French press, the nutty flavour profile of this coffee makes for a delicious cup, either with milk or black.  
  Recommended Resting Period:     15 Days

Name: Dhak Blend
Desc:
Our  Dhak Blend  is an ode to one of our favourite Indian trees with its colorful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring. The coffees used in this blend are naturally processed which means that the  coffee beans  are dried with the cherry, resulting in complex, fruity and sweet flavours. 
 Roasted dark to bring out flavours of dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste. 
 Our roasting team recommends the Dhak Blend for espresso-based drinks as well as manual brews such as the Moka Pot and the French Press. 
   Recommended Resting Period:     9 Days

Name: Attikan Estate
Tasting_Notes: Attikan
Desc:
Attikan Estate’s arabica  coffee beans  come from the Biligiriranga Hills in Karnataka and make for one of our most popular coffees. Sweet with nutty overtones and balanced acidity, this is the darkest of our standard medium roasts and recommended for espresso lovers. It is a versatile coffee that also works for manual brewing methods such as Moka Pot, South Indian Filter and AeroPress.  
 Located to the south of Mysore, the Biligiriranga Hills, or ‘white hills’ are named after the mist that hangs over the region. At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees.

Name: Mooleh Manay Estate – CM Natural
Tasting_Notes: Returning to our
Desc:
Returning to our Producer Series after 2023, Komal Sable and Akshay Dashrath share their first experiment with carbonic maceration. Building on the clarity and consistency they achieved with anaerobic fermentation last season, the fifth-generation producers modified their drums to create a CO₂-rich, oxygen-free environment that allows for slower, more controlled fermentation within whole cherries.  
 The process began by removing floaters to select only ripe, dense cherries, followed by a brief pre-drying phase to reduce surface moisture. The cherries were then sealed in drums, and a custom culture was introduced to extend the fermentation. Over 60 hours, this combination of carbonic maceration and yeast inoculation ensured thorough mucilage breakdown and the development of deep complexity.  
 Post-fermentation, the cherries were dried on raised beds inside a polyhouse. Continuous raking over 7 to 10 days ensured even drying until a final moisture level of 11–12% was reached.  
 Roasted light by Rishab from our team, this coffee offers a well-structured cup with notes of fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness. It opens with the aroma of mixed berries and carries a syrupy mouthfeel, with layered flavours of dried fig, plum, black grape, and mulberry. A chocolatey aftertaste marks the finish, adding further depth.  
 We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    16  Days  
   Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

Name: 13th Birthday Blend
Desc:
This celebratory blend brings together natural lots from Stanmore, Orchardale, and Riverdale Estates in Yercaud, along with a washed lot from Unakki Estate in Chikmagalur, which forms the base. Its flavour profile takes us back to the Black Forest cakes many of us celebrated birthdays with during our teen years.  
 Opening with the aroma of honey and strawberries, the cup has a medium-high body and a round mouthfeel. You'll notice notes of strawberry, chocolate, cherry, and pear, followed by a lingering finish of chocolate-covered strawberries.  
 This blend brews well across a range of methods, including espresso, AeroPress, French Press, Moka Pot, and Pour Over. Equally enjoyable black or with milk, it lends itself to a wide range of recipes. 
   Recommended Resting Period:     10   Days

Name: SKIA Coffee (Pack of 2)
Desc:
This two-pack (100 gms each) brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg. Grown by smallholder farmers and processed by Ashish Rao, a first-generation producer, these lots mark our first collaboration with Skia Coffee.  
 Ripe, high-density cherries were pulped with the mucilage left intact, then placed in sealed tanks for a 72-hour anaerobic fermentation. A yeast strain purpose-built for controlled fermentation was introduced during this stage to develop complexity.  
 From there, the two lots took separate paths.  
  Honey Sun Dried    
 The first lot was dried slowly on raised beds under controlled shade. Roasted to a medium profile, it makes for a balanced cup with notes of sweet lime, prunes, and almond.  
  Recommended Resting Period:  16 Days 
  Thermal Shock    
 This second lot was immersed in hot water, then rapidly cooled in ice. It was then mechanically washed and dried slowly under shade. Also roasted to a medium profile, it brews cups with notes of tangerine, brown sugar, and berries.   
 Both coffees brew beautifully as an espresso or with an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. They taste great black and pair well with milk. Together, they offer a chance to explore how thoughtful shifts in processing shape flavour in the final cup.   
  Recommended Resting Period:  12 Days 
  Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

Name: Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective
Tasting_Notes: It's always exciting for us to partner with a new
Desc:
It's always exciting for us to partner with a new farm. With Meghalaya's Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective, that excitement runs even deeper. A completely new coffee growing region for us, it speaks of the possibilities that the North East Indian soil holds for specialty production. The collective’s origin goes back a decade, when Daman, a first-generation coffee producer, visited Nongryniang—a remote village in Khasi Hills and home to the nanny who cared for him in his early years.  
 " There, nestled among the misty hills, I came across two old coffee plants growing in someone’s backyard. I later learned that back in the 1980s, the government had briefly launched a coffee planting program in the area. Like many such initiatives, it had long been abandoned and forgotten. But those plants stayed with me. And so did the people .", he recounts. Since then, Daman started a decade-long pursuit of craft and community. From shading systems to post-harvest processing, he spent years learning all it takes to grow high-quality coffee. Over time, the collective has grown in both, resolve and numbers, with 75 farmers now contributing to a harvest. They pick only the ripest cherries by hand, which are sun-dried for 15–22 days depending on weather conditions.   
 The first coffee that we’ve sourced from the collective is a natural lot we’ve chosen to roast to a medium profile. It brews cups that open with the aroma of raisins, unfolding into a creamy mouthfeel. Notes of blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish. A balanced coffee, it lends well to various brewing methods, including espresso, Moka Pot, French Press, and AeroPress. It is enjoyable on its own as well as in milk-based beverages. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    13  Days

Name: Ratnagiri Estate - Dark Room Natural
Tasting_Notes: Our latest release from Ratnagiri
Desc:
Our latest release from Ratnagiri Estate showcases a new frontier in controlled processing. It was shaped by a 60-hour fermentation with a custom culture, then dried slowly for 13 days in the estate’s climate-controlled dark room. 
 A rare facility found at only a handful of estates worldwide, the dark room is fully sealed and fitted with precision racks. It holds temperature between 2°C and 30°C and maintains humidity at 10%. Slow drying with this level of control deepens flavour, preserves sweetness, and brings clarity to the cup. 
 Antony, our roaster, approached the roast with a carefully extended Maillard phase to build natural sweetness, finishing light to let the coffee’s character shine. The result is a sparkling wine-like cup with a silky body and a bright mouthfeel. It opens with the aroma of strawberry and prune. Notes of passionfruit, mosambi, pineapple, and black tea follow, with the tea-like note carrying through the finish. 
 For the best experience, we suggest brewing this limited-edition lot as a Pour Over or using an AeroPress. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    8    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Kalledevarapura Estate - The Fermentation Edit
Tasting_Notes: Meet our
Process: natural, used to benchmark the inoculated lots
Desc:
Meet our roasters’ favourite experiment from Nano-X ’25. 
 To create this special five-pack, we played with a whole spectrum of microorganisms, from homegrown kombucha to lab-cultured strains. Working with a local laboratory, the producer, Shravan, curated a diverse range of cultures, while Tyler, our Head of Roastery, prepared a robust batch of active kombucha using black tea and raw sugar. 
 Ripe coffee cherries were split into eleven barrels of 120 kg each, with inoculants gradually added to ten barrels while one was kept as a control. The barrels were sealed and left indoors for a 72-hour fermentation, with the kombucha batch opened after 24 hours to allow oxygen exposure, as the SCOBY (Symbiotic Culture of Bacteria and Yeast) requires it to remain active. Once fermentation was complete, the cherries were dried on raised beds for 20 to 25 days. 
 This limited-release brings together the highest-scoring samples from the experiment. It includes lots fermented with: 
 Homegrown Kombucha, creating a cup with notes of plum, raw mango, candy apple, and goji berries. 
 Saccharomyces cerevisiae, building an expressive coffee with notes of white nectarine, pomegranate, roasted hazelnut, and pomelo. 
 Pichia yeast, developing a clean cup with notes of cane sugar, green apple, jaggery, and roasted almonds. 
 Lactic acid bacteria, which shaped a coffee with notes of orange zest, black raisin, wild honey, and cocoa. 
 An anaerobically processed natural, used to benchmark the inoculated lots. It brews cups with hints of florality and notes of lemonade, roasted almond, and green grape. 
 We recommend drinking these coffees black, brewed as Pour Overs or using the AeroPress. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    12    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Riverdale Estate - White Rose
Tasting_Notes: Fermented with rose petals, this layered light
Desc:
Fermented with rose petals, this layered light roast perfectly embodies why Riverdale Estate is a pioneer in experimental processing. 
 Only the ripest cherries, hand-picked from the higher-altitude blocks of the farm, where the fruit matures slowly and develops an enhanced sweetness, were used. Once harvested, the cherries underwent a triple wash with natural spring water to remove impurities. 
 After removing floaters, rose petals were introduced during fermentation, setting up the stage for complexity. The cherries were then slow-dried on raised beds for up to 30 days, allowing for even drying. Finally, the coffee was hulled at the estate’s dry mill, where any defective beans were eliminated before being sent to our roastery. 
 The result is a gently perfumed cup with bright notes of plum, pomegranate, strawberry and orange blossom, complemented by a smooth mouthfeel and a lingering sweetness. 
 We recommend brewing it black using an AeroPress or as a Pour Over. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    14  Days  
     Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Amruthavarshini Estate
Tasting_Notes: Meet our second release by Amruthavarshini
Process: using the anaerobic natural method, this medium
Desc:
Meet our second release by Amruthavarshini Estate, a women-led estate run by a mother-daughter duo. Processed using the anaerobic natural method, this medium roast brews fruity and nutty cups with a pleasant sweetness.   
 A honey-like aroma leads into bright notes of cherries and pineapples. The nuttiness of roasted almonds adds depth, while the mouthfeel remains syrupy. In the finish, you’ll taste the lingering aftertaste of raisins and nuts.   
 Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. It tastes great whether you enjoy it black or with milk. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    12    Days

Name: Breakfast Blend - Medium Roast - Stoned fruits with caramel overtones
Tasting_Notes: Breakfast Blend is a Medium
Desc:
Breakfast Blend is a Medium Roast, Naturally processed coffee which stands out with interesting fruity notes and sweet aroma in the cup.  
  We recommend this elegant & refreshing coffee as the first cup in the morning & so we named it as the “Breakfast Blend”.  
  Like all our other coffees this coffee too is proudly grown in India, on the farms of Chikamagalur at an altitude of 3000 ft above sea level.  
  Breakfast blend has very interesting Flavor profile with notes of Stoned Fruits and Caramel overtones giving a balanced mouthfeel and texture to the final cup.  
  It is best enjoyed as black with Pour Overs and Aeropress but it goes really well with milk based drink too!

Name: Coal Black - Aura estate
Tasting_Notes: Molasses • Cocoa nibs/Toasted nuts • Passion fruit
Desc:
Aura Farming – Banana Washed Process. Grown at 3700ft above sea level, Coal Black is crafted from Coffee cherries are harvested at a minimum ripeness level of above 95%. After harvesting, the cherries are washed, and all floating fruits are removed to ensure quality selection. These cherries are kept in an anaerobic natural fermentation in a container for 24 hours. The coffee fruits are then pulped and transferred to a container arranged layer by layer with banana leaves, where they are kept for 48 hours of fermentation, during which pH, temperature, and humidity are controlled. Finally, after fermentation, the coffee fruits are washed and transferred to raised beds, where they are slowly dried for 18 Days. During the drying period, temperature and relative humidity are carefully monitored and maintained to ensure uniform drying and preserve coffee quality.  
  Tasting Notes:   
  Molasses • Cocoa nibs/Toasted nuts • Passion fruit

Name: Silver Lining - Aura estate
Tasting_Notes: Green Apple • Cherry • Agave Amica
Desc:
Aura Farming – Anaerobic Naturals Process. Grown at 3700ft above sea level, the coffee fruits were harvested at a minimum ripeness of 97%, with a Brix level above 26%. After harvesting, the fruits were washed and the floaters were removed. The selected fruits were then kept in water for 48 hours, with the temperature maintained below 10°C. After draining the water, the coffee fruits were fermented anaerobically for 8 days in a dark, closed room, ensuring the temperature did not cross 10°C. Once the fermentation was completed, the fruits were moved to raised beds and dried in a dark room for 25 days. During this drying period, the coffee cherries were packed in bags and kept in the dark room at night, and every morning they were placed back on the raised beds to continue drying.  
  Tasting Notes:   
  Green Apple • Cherry • Agave Amica

Name: CITRUS CIRCUS
Tasting_Notes: Citrus Circus A red honey
Desc:
Citrus Circus 
 A red honey processed coffee from Koraput, Odisha, roasted as a true omni roast for both filter and espresso. 
 Citrus Circus is playful but precise. Bright citrus sweetness meets jammy depth, balancing candy-like fruit with brown sugar warmth. It’s expressive without being loud, juicy without losing structure. 
 Taste Profile 
  Filter  Orange candy and raisin jam upfront, layered with brown sugar sweetness and mixed berries. Soft citrus peel rounds the cup, finishing clean, juicy, and gently sweet like citrus candy. 
  Espresso  Thick marmalade sweetness with a brown sugar body. Jammy fruit carries through the shot, supported by soft berry acidity and a smooth, lingering finish. 
 Brew Recipes 
  V60  
 Coffee: 15 g Water: 240 ml Ratio: 1:16 Temperature: 92–94°C Grind: Medium Brew Time: 2:30–3:00 
 Results in a bright, candy-like cup with layered sweetness and a clean citrus finish. 
  Espresso  
 Dose: 18 g Yield: 38–40 g Time: 28–32 seconds Ratio: ~1:2.1 
 Juicy marmalade body with soft acidity and a rounded, sugar-sweetig sweetness. 
 Details 
 Origin: Koraput, Odisha Varietal: 795 Process: Red Honey Roast: Medium Omni Brew: Filter & Espresso 
 Lively without chaos. Sweet without sharpness.  Citrus Circus  is controlled brightness, performed perfectly.

Name: COZY COOKIE
Tasting_Notes: Cozy Cookie A washed coffee from Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia
Desc:
Cozy Cookie  
 A washed coffee from Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, roasted as a balanced omni roast for both filter and espresso. 
  Cozy Cookie  is warm, smooth, and comforting by design. Built around sweetness and body rather than acidity, it brings together cocoa, nuts, and soft vanilla notes in a cup that feels familiar and easy. It’s gentle without being boring, sweet without being heavy. 
 
  Taste Profile  
  Filter  
 Cocoa and roasted nuts lead the cup, followed by soft vanilla sweetness. The profile stays round and smooth with low acidity, finishing clean and cozy with a lingering chocolatey warmth. 
  Espresso  
 Caramel cookie sweetness with a chocolate-forward body. Thick, creamy, and dessert-like, supported by malted vanilla notes and a smooth, lingering finish. Especially good with milk. 
 
  Brew Recipes  
  V60  
 Coffee: 15 g Water: 240 ml Ratio: 1:16 Temperature: 92–94°C Grind: Medium Brew Time: 2:30–3:00 
 Results in a smooth, cocoa-driven cup with gentle sweetness and a calm, comforting finish. 
  Espresso  
 Dose: 18 g Yield: 38–40 g Time: 28–32 seconds Ratio: ~1:2.1 
 Creamy, chocolatey espresso with caramel cookie sweetness and a rounded mouthfeel. 
 
  Details  
 Origin: Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia Varietal: Mixed Heirloom Process: Washed Roast: Medium Omni Brew: Filter & Espresso

Name: DARK HONEY
Tasting_Notes: Honeyed Apricot, Dried Figs, Wildflower Nectar
Desc:
Chikmagalur, KA | SLN 795 | Dark Honey Process | 100% Arabica  
 This one’s for those who chase depth. 
 Sourced from the lush slopes of Unnaki Estate, this Arabica is processed using the Dark Honey method where part of the mucilage is left intact during drying, letting natural sugars soak into the bean. What you get is a cup bursting with golden complexity. 
 Think: honeyed apricot, dried figs, and a soft wildflower nectar finish. 
 Roasted medium to keep the balance between fruit and body. Smooth acidity, full texture, and a lingering sweetness that doesn’t quit. 
  Tasting Notes:  Honeyed Apricot · Dried Figs · Wildflower Nectar 
  Elevation:  4000–4700 FT  Process:  Dark Honey  Roast Level:  Medium  Varietal:  SLN 795

Name: DARK MATTER
Tasting_Notes: Most coffee is overhyped and underdelive
Desc:
Most coffee is overhyped and underdelivers. 
 Too acidic. Too inconsistent. Too much talk. 
  Dark Matter fixes that.  
 Roasted deeper for strength, body, and reliability — this is coffee that hits the same way, every single day. No surprises. No adjustments. Just a solid, satisfying cup that works whether you drink it black or with milk.

   Why This Works   
 
 Built for  daily drinking , not occasional tasting 
 
 Low acidity  — easy on the stomach 
 
 Consistent every brew  — no guesswork 
 Strong enough for milk, clean enough for black 
 
 This is the coffee you don’t think about. You just reach for it. 
 
   Brew Recipes   
   V60   
 Coffee: 15 g Water: 240 ml Ratio: 1:16 Temperature: 93–95°C Grind: Medium Brew Time: 2:30–3:00

   Espresso   
 Dose: 18 g Yield: 36–40 g Time: 28–32 seconds Ratio: ~1:2 
 Thick, chocolate-forward espresso with high body and long finish. 
 
   Details   
 Origin: India Varietal: Blend Process: Multi-Process Roast: Vienna (Medium-Dark) Brew: Filter & Espresso 
 
 If your coffee needs too much effort to taste good, it’s not good coffee. 
  Dark Matter is built to work.

Name: DRIFTWOOD
Tasting_Notes: DRIFTWOOD Medium
Process: it’s a ritual. At BROOT, we craft each
Desc:
DRIFTWOOD 
 Medium Roast Monsoon Malabar 
 There’s something strangely comforting about Monsoon Malabar. 
 Maybe it’s the way the coffee changes with time. Maybe it’s the sea air. Or maybe it’s because no other coffee tastes this unmistakably Indian. 
 DRIFTWOOD is our medium roast take on the classic Monsoon Malabar profile. Instead of pushing it too dark, we roasted it slower and lighter to preserve its dense body while bringing out more sweetness, texture, and clarity in the cup. 
 The result is low in acidity, syrupy, woody, slightly spiced, and incredibly smooth. 
 Expect notes of cocoa nibs, toasted nuts, old cedar wood, and mellow raisin sweetness layered over that iconic monsooned depth. 
 This is the kind of coffee that feels best during slow evenings, rain outside the window, or the first quiet cup of the day. 
 Heavy body. Soft bitterness. Long comforting finish. 
 
 Taste Profile 
 Filter 
 Cocoa nibs • toasted nuts • wet wood 
 Espresso 
 Dark chocolate • raisin • tobacco sweetness 
 
 Origin 
  Region  Chikkamagalur, Karnataka 
  Elevation  1200 MSL 
  Variety  SLN 795 
  Process  Traditional Monsooning 
 
 Roast Level 
 Medium Roast 
 Built to retain the signature body of Monsoon Malabar while opening up a smoother and sweeter side of the coffee. 
 
 Best Brewed As 
 
 
 Espresso 
 
 
 Moka Pot 
 
 
 French Press 
 
 
 AeroPress 
 
 
 Milk-based drinks 
 
 
 
 Brew Guide 
 Pour Over 
 18g coffee 300g water 93°C 2:45–3:00 mins 
 Espresso 
 18g in 38–40g out 28–32 sec 
 
 What Monsooning Does 
 During monsooning, the beans are exposed to humid monsoon winds along India’s western coast for weeks. The coffee swells in size, loses acidity, deepens in body, and develops the earthy, mellow character that made Monsoon Malabar famous around the world. 
 DRIFTWOOD keeps that heritage intact, just with a cleaner and more modern roast approach.

Tasting_Notes: Warm Cocoa • Brown Sugar • A Familiar Finish A balanced, full-bodied espresso blend designed for everyday comfort
Process: it’s a ritual. At BROOT, we craft each
Desc:
Warm Cocoa • Brown Sugar • A Familiar Finish A balanced, full-bodied espresso blend designed for everyday comfort. 
 House No. 02 is the second release in our House Series — a lineup of coffees built around routine, consistency, and quiet familiarity. 
 Built on a washed base from Chikamagalur, layered with arabica cherry for body, and finished with a touch of natural sweetness from Kaimara, this blend is smooth, rounded, and deeply satisfying. 
 Expect a cup that leans into warmth soft cocoa notes, gentle brown sugar sweetness, and a full, comforting body that holds beautifully across brew styles. It’s easy to drink, easy to dial in, and hard to replace once you get used to it. 
 Designed for everyday use, House No. 02 performs just as well with milk as it does black. Whether it’s your morning espresso or an evening cup, this is the kind of coffee you reach for without thinking. 
 
  The House Series  
 House No. 02 continues our House Series, coffees designed to be part of your everyday. 
 Every fourth drop introduces a new House blend. Not one-offs, but evolving expressions of what a daily coffee can be. 
 House No. 01 set the foundation. House No. 02 builds on it, fuller, smoother, more refined. 
 With House No. 03, 04 and beyond, the idea remains the same: different expressions, same purpose. 
 Built to stay. Refined over time. 
 
  Why you’ll love it  
 • Smooth, full-bodied cup with low to medium acidity • Warm cocoa profile with a soft, natural sweetness • Excellent crema and texture for espresso • Works beautifully with milk and black brews • Balanced and easy to dial in across methods 
 
  Brew Guide  
 Works best for: 
 Espresso Moka Pot French Press South Indian Filter Manual Pour Over (for a fuller, richer cup) 
 
  Roast Level  
 Medium to Medium Dark Roast

 If you enjoy balanced coffees with a warm, chocolate-forward profile and a smooth, comforting finish—House No. 02 is built for your everyday.

Name: Jam Jar
Tasting_Notes: Jam Jar A naturally
Desc:
Jam Jar 
 A naturally processed  Typica  from  Lam Dong, Vietnam , roasted for both filter and espresso. 
 Jam Jar is rich, composed, and fruit-forward. Built around depth rather than brightness, it delivers syrupy sweetness with a clean, elegant finish. 
 Taste Profile 
  Filter  Juicy, jam-forward cup with honeyed sweetness and a refined cocoa finish. 
  Espresso  Strawberry jam and dark fudge, layered with panela sweetness and a soft floral lift on the finish. 
 Brew Recipes 
  V60  
 
 
 Coffee: 15 g 
 
 
 Water: 240 ml 
 
 
 Ratio: 1:16 
 
 
 Temperature: 92–94°C 
 
 
 Grind: Medium 
 
 
 Brew Time: 2:30–3:00 
 
 
 Results in a juicy, rounded cup with clear sweetness and a clean cocoa finish. 
  Espresso  
 
 
 Dose: 18 g 
 
 
 Yield: 40–42 g 
 
 
 Time: 28–32 seconds 
 
 
 Ratio: ~1:2.2 
 
 
 Thick body, syrupy sweetness, jammy fruit upfront with a polished finish. 
 Details 
 
 
  Origin:  Lam Dong, Vietnam 
 
 
  Varietal:  Typica 
 
 
  Process:  Natural 
 
 
  Roast:  Medium 
 
 
  Brew:  Filter & Espresso 
 
 
 Bold without excess. Sweet without noise. Jam Jar is restraint, refined.

Name: MALTLINE
Tasting_Notes: coffee
Desc:
MALTLINE 
 Some coffees taste like coffee. 
 MALTLINE tastes like someone accidentally left a pint of craft beer beside a brew bar and discovered something special. 
 Produced at Kaapikaadu Estate, this lot underwent a Kölsch beer fermentation before drying, creating a cup that blurs the line between specialty coffee and brewing culture. The result isn't beer-flavoured coffee. It's coffee with an entirely different kind of sweetness, structure and complexity. 
 Expect layers of malted biscuit, golden raisin and dark honey on filter. Pull it as espresso and it transforms into notes of toffee, stout cacao and brown sugar, wrapped in a syrupy body with remarkably low bitterness. 
 This is the second release in our experimental robusta series and one of the most unusual coffees we've roasted to date. 
 If you've never enjoyed robusta before, start here. 
 
 IN THE CUP 
  Filter  Malted Biscuit • Golden Raisin • Dark Honey 
  Espresso  Toffee • Stout Cacao • Brown Sugar 
 
 WHY IT'S DIFFERENT 
 Most robustas are selected for caffeine and body. 
 This one was selected for flavour. 
 The Kölsch beer fermentation introduces a deeper sweetness and a rounded, malt-like character while preserving the heavy mouthfeel robusta is known for. The cup is rich, comforting and surprisingly refined, with almost no harshness and a long lingering finish. Fermentation, processing and roast all shape the final flavour experience in specialty coffee.    
 
 COFFEE DETAILS 
  Producer:  Kaapikaadu Estate  Region:  Karnataka, India  Process:  Kölsch Beer Fermented Natural  Species:  Canephora (Robusta)  Roast Level:  Medium-Light  Best For:  Espresso, Moka Pot, AeroPress, French Press, Pour Over 
 
 FOR PEOPLE WHO... 
 ✓ Love dark beers, stouts and barrel-aged drinks 
 ✓ Want a coffee with huge body and sweetness 
 ✓ Think robusta deserves a second chance 
 ✓ Enjoy coffees that start conversations 
  Limited Release. Once this lot is gone, it's gone.

Name: MIDNIGHT EQUATOR
Tasting_Notes: Midnight Equator A carbonic maceration natural from Uganda
Desc:
Midnight Equator 
 A carbonic maceration natural from Uganda, roasted medium to medium-light as a true omni roast. 
 Midnight Equator is precise fermentation done right. The sealed-tank process intensifies fruit clarity while preserving structure, giving the cup layered sweetness without chaos. 
 Dark fruit leads. Cocoa grounds it. The finish lingers long and composed.
