Name: MOJITO
Tasting_Notes: This lot from Melkodige
Process: it’s a ritual. At BROOT, we craft each
Desc:
This lot from Melkodige Estate is our kind of experiment done right. Ripe SL9 cherries were hand-picked, floated to remove lights, then submerged with EM5 microbes for a 74-hour anaerobic ferment. After that, the cherries were moved to raised wooden trays and dried under shade for 15 days. 
 What this really means is flavor with layers: cocoa and raisin at the core, a lift of sweet lime, and a finish that hints at cacao nib and dried dates. It’s juicy without getting wild, sweet without tasting candy-like. 
 We roast this medium-light to keep the lime sparkle and retain the chocolatey depth that makes the cup feel complete. If you’re into expressive naturals that still behave well on brew bar, this is the one. 
 Taste 
 Cocoa, raisin, sweet lime, cacao nib, dried dates. 
 Brew guide 
 
 
 Filter: 1:16, 92–94°C, 2:45–3:00 total (V60/Kalita/AeroPress). 
 
 
 Light espresso: 1:2.3 in 30–34s; expect a syrupy shot with citrus pop. 
 
 
 Specs 
 
 
 Estate: Melkodige Estate, Chikmagalur, KA 
 
 
 Variety: SL9 
 
 
 Process: EM5 anaerobic natural (74-hour submerged ferment) 
 
 
 Drying: 15 days on raised, shaded beds 
 
 
 Elevation: 4200 ft MSL 
 
 
 Roast: Medium-Light 
 
 
 Best for: Filter, pourover, AeroPress; adventurous light espresso 
 
 
 Freshness: Roasted to order. Peak from day 7–28. Reseal tight.

Name: OBSIDIAN
Tasting_Notes: Obsidian Ammikulavi
Desc:
Obsidian 
  Ammikulavi Estate • 96hr Anaerobic Canephora • Medium Light Roast  
 Some coffees impress you on the first sip. 
 Obsidian makes you question everything you thought you knew about robusta. 
 Sourced from the mist-covered hills of the Ammikulavi Estate, this 96-hour anaerobic lot is our first release in the Robusta Series. It is rich, fruit-forward, and remarkably refined, showcasing a side of robusta that most coffee drinkers never get to experience. 
 In the filter, Obsidian opens with notes of black grape, aged rum, and dried fig, wrapped in a syrupy body that lingers long after the cup is empty. As espresso, it transforms into layers of molasses, dark cacao, and burnt sugar, producing a dense crema and a deeply satisfying finish. 
 Roasted medium-light to preserve its fermentation character and natural sweetness, Obsidian delivers complexity without harshness and intensity without bitterness. 
 This is not a coffee we launched because it's different. 
 We launched it because it's genuinely delicious. 
 Filter Impression 
  Black Grape • Aged Rum • Dried Fig  
 Espresso Impression 
  Molasses • Dark Cacao • Burnt Sugar  
 Origin 
  Estate:  Ammikulavi Estate  Region:  Tamil Nadu, India  Elevation:  1300–1400 MASL  Species:  Canephora  Process:  96hr Anaerobic Fermentation  Roast Level:  Medium Light 
 Brew Guide 
  Filter • AeroPress • Clever Dripper • French Press • Espresso  
 Roaster's Note 
 For decades, robusta has been judged by its worst examples. Obsidian is what happens when the species is treated with the same care, intention, and craftsmanship as the world's finest coffees. 
 One sip is usually enough to change someone's mind. ☕️

Name: RATNAGIRI NATURAL CUT
Tasting_Notes: Fruity • Jammy • Wild Ratnagiri Natural Cut is where things get interesting
Desc:
Fruity • Jammy • Wild  
 Ratnagiri Natural Cut is where things get interesting. 
 This is coffee pushed to its expressive edge—bold fruit notes, fermented sweetness, and a heavier body that lingers long after the last sip. It’s not subtle, and it’s not trying to be. 
 Expect bursts of juicy red fruits, syrupy sweetness, and a slightly wild finish that makes every cup feel alive. This is the kind of coffee that stands out instantly—loud, complex, and unapologetically different. 
 Not for everyone. But unforgettable for the right palate. 
 
 What to Expect 
 
 Juicy, fruit-forward profile 
 Jammy sweetness with depth 
 Heavy body with lingering finish 
 Slightly funky, experimental character 
 
 
  Details 
 
 
 Origin:  Ratnagiri Estate, India 
 
 Process:  Natural 
 
 Varietal:  SLN 9 
 
 Roast Level:  Medium 
 
 Best For:  Pour Over, Aeropress, Espresso (for adventurous shots) 
 
 
 Why You’ll Love It 
 If you enjoy coffees that push boundaries and surprise you every sip—this is exactly that.

Name: Attikan Estate - Cultured Naturals
Tasting_Notes: Strawberry, Red Wine, Black Grapes, Chamomile
Desc:
From the high-altitude slopes of Attikan Estate comes an   exclusive natural microlot   that’s as expressive as it is elegant. The natural process brings out a   vivid fruit-forward character  , and we knew the roast had to preserve every layer of its complexity.  
  We chose a   gentle light roast   to let the coffee’s natural vibrancy shine—drawing out the   bright strawberry and black grape notes   while allowing a   subtle red wine complexity   to develop in the cup. The creamy body adds depth and smoothness, balancing the   medium acidity   so the coffee feels both lively and refined.  
  As the cup cools, delicate   floral whispers of chamomile   appear, rounding off the experience with a graceful finish. This is a coffee we treated with restraint and precision in the roaster, ensuring every nuance of its natural processing and terroir could express itself fully.  
   Information:  
  Estate:  Attikan Estate 
  Region:  Biligiri Hills, Karnataka 
  Producer:  Hamsini & Sriram Appadurai 
  Varietal:  SLN 9, HDT*Catuai 
  Lot:  Microlot 
  Process:  Cultured Naturals (Lactobacillus + Pichia Fermentation) 
  Roast Level:  Light 
  Tasting Notes:  Strawberry, Red Wine, Black Grapes, Chamomile 
  Best Brewed with:  Pour Over, Clever Dripper, Aeropress, French Press

Name: BAARBARA BRANDY BARREL AGED
Tasting_Notes: Caramelised Finish
Desc:
Boozy Berry. Oak. Caramelised Finish. Like dessert and a nightcap in the same cup    
   Estate:   Baarabara Estate 
    Origin:   Chikmagalur, Karnataka  
   Roast:        Medium Roast 
   Process:   Brandy Barrel Aged  
  THIS IS FOR YOU, IF  
  you like rich coffees with a boozy edge     you enjoy dark fruit and dessert-like sweetness     you want something bold, smooth and slightly wild  
  BREW GUIDE  
  The Classic Press Recipe  
 
 
  0:00:   Add 250g of water and stir gently.  
 
 
  0:30:   Place the lid on and let it steep.  
 
 
  4:00:     Press slowly and serve immediately.  
 
 
  Target Time:   4m 00s – 4m 30s.  
 
 
  Jammy berries, oak and a deep caramel finish.  
  The Inverted AeroPress Recipe  
 
 
  0:00:     Add 220g of water and stir gently.  
 
 
  0:30:     Attach the cap and let it steep.  
 
 
  2:00:     Flip and press slowly for 30 seconds.  
 
 
  Target Time:   2m 30s.  
 
 
  Rounder body, boozy sweetness, softer finish.

Name: BAARBARA RUM BARREL AGED
Tasting_Notes: Rum. Molasses. Raisins. Dark fruit, boozy, smooth finish
Process: Brandy Barrel Aged THIS IS FOR YOU, IF you like spirit-forward coffees you enjoy deeper, fruit-led
Desc:
Rum. Molasses. Raisins. Dark fruit, boozy, smooth finish     
   Estate:   Baarabara Estate 
    Origin:   Chikmagalur, Karnataka  
   Roast:        Medium Roast 
   Process:   Brandy Barrel Aged  
  THIS IS FOR YOU, IF  
  you like spirit-forward coffees     you enjoy deeper, fruit-led flavour profiles     you want something smooth with a slightly boozy edge  
  BREW GUIDE  
  The Overnight Cold Brew Recipe  
 
 
  0:00:   Add 60g coffee to 700g cold water.  
 
 
  0:10:   Stir gently to make sure all grounds are saturated.  
 
 
  12:00:   Strain and serve over ice.  
 
 
  Target Time:   12–14 hours steep.  
 
 
  Smooth, mellow and rum-like with notes of dark fruit.  
  The Iced Pour Over Recipe  
 
 
  0:00 (Bloom):   Pour 50g of water. Wait 45 seconds.  
 
 
  0:45:   Pour up to 150g.  
 
 
  1:30:   Final pour up to 200g directly over ice.  
 
 
  Target Time:   2m 30s – 2m 50s.  
 
 
  Bright, boozy and crisp with a raisiny finish.

This edition unfolds as a three-course coffee journey, each course paired with a thoughtfully crafted vegetarian dish designed to mirror the coffee’s mood, process, and sensory arc.

Name: Tricolate Coffee Brewer
Desc:
The Right Conditions for High Extractions 
 Taking inspiration from precision pouring accessories and flat-bed brewers alike, the Tricolate offers more control over flow rate, agitation, and percolation than most brewers and significantly reduces the possibility of channeling. This is achieved by a combination of elements, including the flat bottom and its form-fitting filter, which eliminate bypass, ensuring that all the liquid in the cup after the brew will contain coffee solids; the wide base (80mm in diameter) and vertical walls, which make for a shallow, even coffee bed that creates the ideal conditions for uniform water-coffee contact; and the dispersion screen, which distributes the water evenly, reducing the likelihood of channeling. The result of such a finely tuned brewing system is high extraction, which translates to the palate as dense flavor. 
 Agitation With Minimal Effort 
 An oft-overlooked aspect of pour-over brewing is the pour itself, which has the dual responsibility of evenly saturating and satisfactorily agitating the coffee grounds with the water. Although this sounds easy, it is not, and is most often helped along by a special gooseneck kettle and a steady hand. Tricolate, however, has removed that one variable from the equation. The precision holes in the Tricolate's dispersion screen control the flow rate, dictating how much water can get through at any given time, and the screen itself, mounted roughly four inches above the base, controls the pour height and therefore the agitation. As a result, it is possible to achieve consistently high extractions with minimal effort and with any kettle. All that is required for a perfect brew is the appropriate grind size and water temperature. The Tricolate will do the rest. 
 Environmentally Sound 
 The Tricolate is made in Australia of Tritan plastic, which is durable, heat-stable, and free from BPA, BPS, or other bisphenols. The German-made filters, a bag of which is included in the package, have a consistent pore structure, another reason for the high extractions, and, being relatively small, are made from less paper than those for traditional pour over brewers, reducing the environmental impact of every brew.

Name: Intenso Fermentation
Tasting_Notes: This nano-lot from Baarbara
Process: Whole Beans / 250 grams is backordered and will ship as soon as it is back in stock. This nano-lot from Baarbara
Desc:
This nano-lot from Baarbara Estate was produced by adding yeast to the ripened cherries in a controlled environment. The fermentation process results in notes of candied fruits and berries in the cup with a prominent acidity and complexity.   
  This is the first year we experiment with yeast fermentation. For this lot, we chose a yeast called Intenso (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), intended to increase fruity flavours, mouthfeel and general cup quality.   
  We found a floral aroma and notes of pomegranate, cherry, candied fruit and a hints of prunes supported by a smooth mouthfeel and the best way to enjoy this is to either brew a pour over or an iced coffee.   
  We have cupped this coffee multiple times in different stages of harvest and roast profiles. It can be strange and puzzling (in a nice way) because the flavours are constantly developing. It's like watching your favourite movie, that you've forgotten.    
   Origin - Single Origin    
   Altitude - 4500 ft - 5000 ft    
   Varietal - SLN 795    
   Roasted for - Filter    
   Best brewed as -Pour Over and Iced Coffees      
   Taste Notes - Pomegranate, Cherry, Candied Fruit & Prunes

Name: Mixed Fruit Fermentation
Tasting_Notes: This nano-lot from Baarbara
Desc:
This nano-lot from Baarbara Estate showcases a unique mixed-fruit fermentation; where handpicked ripened cherries are washed in natural spring water and fermented alongside pineapple, papaya, and watermelon in stainless steel tanks. The process is closely monitored for pH and temperature to ensure consistency, with a 1:2 coffee-to-fruit ratio enhancing complexity. Once fermentation is complete, the pulped coffee is sun-dried on raised beds to achieve the perfect moisture level. The result is a lively, tropical coffee with notes of pineapple, honey, sweet lime, and tangerine; offering both brightness and balance in the cup. Our favourite lot this year - we also like to call it a Fruit Punch!    
   Origin - Baarbara, Chikmagalur, Karnataka   
   Altitude - 4500 ft - 5000 ft   
   Varietal - SLN 795   
   Roasted for - Filter    
   Recommended Brewing Equipment - Pour Over (V60/Kalita), Aeropress     
   Taste Notes - Pineapple, Honey, Sweet Lime, Tangerine

Name: Garnet Vin Doux - Roasted on 26/05
Desc:
Grown along the outer slopes of the    Palani Hills at 4200 ft , this lot represents a precise approach to Robusta processing from    Ammikulavi Estate , Tamil Nadu. The estate spans 40 acres, where Arabicas occupy the central terrain and Robustas border the edges. 
 Under the direction of    Darshan , a sixth-generation grower and first-generation specialty processor, this coffee undergoes    anaerobic natural fermentation —a sealed environment that intensifies fruit complexity while refining mouthfeel and sweetness. 
 When brewed at    89°C  for  2 1/2 mins using an AeroPress , the cup reveals a balanced, structured profile: 
 
 
 Aromatics:    Ferment-driven winey notes with subtle spice 
 
 Flavor:   Winey, D ark chocolate, prunes, and caramel sweetness. 
 
 Body:    Full, syrupy texture with clean finish. 
 
 Acidity:    Low and integrated, enhancing perceived sweetness. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Taste Profile  -  Winey, Dark Chocolate,  Prunes, Caramel 
 
 
 
 Origin  -   Ammikulavi Estate, Pulneys, TN 
 
 
 
 Processing  - Anaerobic Naturals 
 
 
 
 Elevation  - 4200 ft 
 
 
 
   Roast:  Medium  Acidity:  Low  Sweetness:  Medium

Name: Kora Zinfandel - Roasted on 01/06
Desc:
We have a new daily favourite for the pour-over lovers in the house 
 At the cupping table, we expected what a well-processed washed coffee typically delivers: clean, chcoolatey, nutty, classic. What we got instead was a cup so fruit-forward it made us double-check the coffee. It's washed, and Ajay, the Q grader, verified this in his cupping notes. 
 This coffee comes from the members of Duduma Farmers Producer Company, rooted in the Lamtaput and Nandapur blocks of Koraput district, Odisha. A community of 841 farmer members — 561 of them coffee growers — 80% from Scheduled Tribes communities,  over 62% women . They don't just grow this coffee. They process it themselves, on their land, with their hands. 
 With the intention to keep the value in the hands of the growers, we don't buy cherries. We source only what the community grows and processes — and when the quality meets specialty grade, we pay accordingly. This harvest earned a 15–20% premium over prevailing market prices. The cup earned it. 
 We roasted this to a medium profile to let the fruitiness come forward cleanly. The result is a cup with gentle acidity, warmth, and just enough complexity to keep you interested — morning or evening, pour-over, Aeropress or even a fruity cold brew. 
  A washed coffee that forgot the rules. Our favourite kind.  
   
 
 
 
  Taste Profile 
 
  
 
 Citrus, Chocolate, Slightly Fruity, Plum like, Nutty  
 
 
 
 
 Origin 
 
    Lamtaput, Koraput, Odisha  
 
 
 
 Processing 
 
  
 Traditional Washed 
 
 
 
 Elevation 
 
     3000+ ft

Name: Maison Mahua - Roasted on 04/06
Desc:
Limited Lot of 30kg only.   In the hills of Punjisil village, on the banks of the  Punjisil Falls , a community of 50 families nurtures this 75 acres of land - 1.5 acres awarded to each beneficiary - an eligible member of the family, harvesting coffee that grows wild among forest cover and stream-fed slopes — where access requires a long, steep walk from the village, and crossing the river stream on foot. 
 Here, harvesting remains a community act, guided by rhythm rather than machinery. Ripe red cherries are hand-carried for over two kilometres, across the river, where they’re de-pulped by a hand-operated pulper, then naturally fermented overnight in the cool, running water of the stream itself. The coffee is then sun-dried on handmade wooden beds, built from locally and seasonally available timber and leaves. Each farmer keeps their parchment at home until moisture is checked and lots are aggregated. 
 Roasted to a medium profile that is suitable for both espresso as well as filter, the resulting cup has a body we fell in love with. It's the kind of cup that you can have everyday, whether as a morning cheer me up, or as a quite wind down at the end of day.  
 
 
 
  Taste Profile 
 
  
 
   
 
 
   
 
     Roasted Nuts, Milk Chocolate, Citrus Zest, Vanilla 
 
 
 
 Origin 
 
   Punjisil, Koraput, Odisha 
 
 
 
 Processing 
 
  
 
   
 
 Traditional Washed 
 
 
 
 Elevation 
 
     3000+ ft

Name: Tawny Ristretta - Roasted on 26/05
Desc:
Limited edition of 45kg   Fine Robustas have always been close to our hearts, and this one adds yet another layer to our journey of discovering truly exceptional lots. 
 Hegbal Estate gets its name for   Hebbagillu -   Kannada for "great gateway". R un by Mr Devdas Menezes since 1996, he is a 3rd generational grower who has pioneered specialty harvests and post harvests for both Arabica and Robusta, and believes in a bright future for Robusta.  
 We got our hands on a beautiful bodied batch - an anaerobic Honey fermented twice for 60 hours. The cherries were stored in Ecotact bags, then pulped, and stored in Ecotact bags again.   After six months of experimentation and five distinct roast profiles, we’ve arrived at this expression — one that best highlights the character of this coffee. We’re releasing it in a limited batch at a special price to invite your palate into the conversation. Your feedback will shape how we take this coffee forward in future roasts.

Name: Trousseau Adwaita - Roasted on 09/06
Desc:
Many coffees promise a great cup. This one has already proven it. 
 Lot A20L13 from Koraput A1 Coffee Estate is a two-time winner of the Flavour of India – Fine Cup Award (2023 & 2024) — not by accident, but by design. Every detail, from harvest to cup, is deliberate. 
 Grown at 3,200 feet in the hills of Koraput, Odisha, the Chandragiri variety here is handled with the kind of care that turns great fruit into something memorable. Ripe cherries are hand-sorted, depulped, and sealed into fermentation tanks for exactly 48 hours. Inside, pH and temperature are tracked closely — controlled microbial activity, balanced sugar breakdown, and layered flavor development without the risk of over-fermentation. 
 What emerges from the tank goes straight to raised drying beds, coated in a rich layer of honey-process mucilage. Sun-dried slowly, turned regularly, and rested before dry milling — this is patience built into every step. 
 In the cup, that patience shows. Strawberry and apple bring brightness upfront. Almond and caramel deepen the mid-palate. A long, sweet finish ties it all together — clean, complex, and unmistakably Chandragiri. 
 Expect this coffee to open up 3 weeks post roast, subject to altitude and local climatic conditions.  
  Recognition:    Flavour of India – Fine Cup Award 2023 & 2024 
 
 
 
 
 Taste Profile  - Strawberry, Almond, Caramel, Apple, Sweet Finish 
 
 
 
 Origin  -   Koraput A1 Coffee Estate, Koraput, Odisha 
 
 
 
 Varietal -  Chandragiri 
 
 
 
 Processing  - 36 hrs Anaerobic Honey Sundried  
 
 
 
 Elevation  - 3200 ft 
 
 
 
   
  Roast:  Light to Medium  Acidity:  Bright  Sweetness:  High 
   Limited edition of 70kg only

Desc: Nestled within the vast scape of the Western Ghats   in India, is the Malnad region of Karnataka, with its rich   heritage, culture and abundance of some   of India’s best coffee plantations. All crops are carefully planted in   between natural and jungle shade tress.

Desc: Our newest specialty coffee is crafted from pulped Arabica beans, fermented for 24 hours in a citronella-based enzymatic solution. The beans are then carefully hand-washed to remove the mucilage and slowly dried to preserve clarity and character. The result is vibrant cup with layered complexity, delicate citrus nuances, and a refined aromatic finish.

Name: Classic Wet Plum
Tasting_Notes: Classic Coffee introduces our new single
Desc:
Classic Coffee introduces our new single-origin microlot from Harley Estate - Wet Plum Coffee 
 Whole ripe cherries are washed with clean water and then stored in an airtight container, for fermentation, along with the introduction of a plum bacteria developed in-house. Post which a slow drying method is adapted to allow the coffee to develop maximum flavours and thereby imparting flavours of a ripe juicy plum. 
   
 Roast Profile : Light to Medium

Name: Classic Whisky Barrel-aged - Cold Brew Bags

Name: THE ROBUSTA SERIES
Desc:
Robusta traditionally has a reputation of being harsh, having stronger & more bitter notes, but we at Harley Estate want to change the perspective by putting a spotlight on Robusta and showcasing all the diverse flavors      that it has to offer, 
  Berry Bounce  
 We start with selectively picking ripe red cherries with a high brix %. Whole cherries are washed with clean water and then stored in an airtight container for fermentation along with yeast developed in-house, which increases the tartness in the final cup. 
  The Monarch  
 We start with selectively picking ripe red cherries with a high Brix %. The best fruits are pulped and slow fermented with a freeze dried in-house yeast & lactic acid bacteria, by varying the fermentation time and the % lactic acid to yeast, we were able to replace the citrus & fruit notes, with sweet hazel nut cream dark cherry & brandy jam. 
  Plume Prince  
 We start with selectively picking ripe red cherries with a high Brix %. Post manual & mechanical sorting and garbling to remove twigs, leaves, floats and other extraneous matters the best fruits are separated. The best fruits are pulped and slow fermented with a freeze dried in-house yeast & lactic acid bacteria. The yeast used & the slow drying bring out a lot of fruitiness in the coffee 
  Thunder Hoof  
 We start with selectively picking ripe red cherries with a high Brix %. The best fruits are pulped and slow fermented with a freeze dried in-house yeast & lactic acid bacteria, by varying the fermentation time and the % lactic acid to yeast, we were able to replace the citrus & fruit notes, with the dark carmel, roasted hazel nut. 
  Sugar Glider  
 We start with selectively picking ripe red cherries with a high brix %. Post manual & mechanical sorting and garbling to remove twigs, leaves, floats and other extraneous matters the best fruits are separated. These are then pulped and taken to a fermentation tank, fermentation process takes place for 36 hours with an in-house aerobic yeast. It is then dried on raised beds till it reaches the desired moisture %

Name: 84 Hours Anoxic Naturals
Desc:
Coffee cherries are hand picked at their peak ripeness to ensure high quality beans. The outer skin is removed using a depulping machine, leaving beans covered in mucilage. Unlike traditional methods, fermentation occurs in oxygen free tanks. The beans ferment in these sealed tanks for about 84 hours, which influences their flavor and aroma. After fermentation, the mucilage remains as the beans are dried on raised beds or patios under controlled conditions for even drying. 
 Located in Chikmagalur, Sai Ashirwad estate is renowned for growing various coffees, including Arabica SLN 795,CxR and Robusta Old Peridenia. The farm has organic certification, showcasing its commitment to sustainable practices. Beyond coffee, it is a haven for wildlife like Indian Gaur and Malabar Giant squirrels. The estate features its own processing unit and drying yards to ensure careful handling of beans. Additionally, water harvesting ponds reflect their focus on environmental stewardship.

Name: Blossom Washed

Desc: This is a 90-hour CULTURE PROCESS washed coffee from the Catuai varietal at our Ratnagiri farm, located at 4,300 feet in the Betamare Patte block. The cherries, with a Brix of 23.2 at harvest, were fermented in stainless-steel fermenters after removing floaters, using a specific strain of yeast and lactic acid bacteria. Following fermentation, they were depulped, washed, and slowly dried on raised beds for 26 days, enhancing their unique flavor profile.

This meticulous approach enhances the unique flavor profile of our coffee.

After harvesting with a Brix of 25.8, we placed the cherries in stainless-steel fermenters, adding a specific strain of yeast and lactic acid bacteria. The fermentation took place in a carbon dioxide-rich environment, followed by a slow drying process on raised beds over 29 days with constant stirring. This meticulous approach enhances the unique flavor profile of our coffee.

Name: Dark Room Naturals
Tasting_Notes: This lot features a unique coffee
Desc: This lot features a unique coffee processing method, starting with thermal shock applied to the cherries to enhance sugar readiness for fermentation. The cherries are then fermented for 48 hours with lactic acid bacteria (LAB) to ensure balanced acidity and optimal flavor development.  After fermentation, they are dried in a dark room for 12 days, minimizing UV degradation and preserving their complexity. The result is a coffee rich in flavor and exceptional quality.

Name: Excelsa community
Process: ing techniques to highlight the finest
Desc:
We hand-pick fully ripe, deep red cherries with high sugar content, ensuring minimal defects and consistent quality. After harvesting, cherries are sorted in water; ripe cherries sink while underripe or damaged ones float and are removed.  Sorted cherries are spread in thin layers on raised beds in a ventilated polyhouse, which controls temperature and protects against rain and UV exposure. We turn the cherries manually to ensure even drying and prevent fermentation. Regular raking promotes airflow, enhancing the final flavor. In the evenings, cherries are covered to shield them from moisture. We monitor moisture levels, aiming for 11–12% to preserve flavors and minimize microbial risks. After drying, cherries are packed in jute sacks and stored for at least two months to stabilize and mature. 
 The Mooleh Manay estate is situated near the scenic backwaters of the Harangi Reservoir in Coorg, Karnataka. It employs a data-oriented strategy for farming and coffee processing, as it believes that data plays a crucial role in enhancing agricultural practices and achieving top-quality coffee production. The estate grows various coffee types, such as Arabica, Robusta, and Excelsa, and utilizes careful processing techniques to highlight the finest flavors. The estate is dedicated to ongoing improvement and innovation and engages in research focused on indigenous Indian Coffea species and soil health.

Name: Flowerette Naturals
Tasting_Notes: During fermentation, we add petals to enhance flavor compounds, resulting in brighter fruit notes with floral
Desc: During fermentation, we add petals to enhance flavor compounds, resulting in brighter fruit notes with floral characteristics. Afterward, we slow-dry the cherries on raised beds for up to 30 days to ensure even drying and improve air circulation. In our dry mill, our quality control team hand-picks any defective beans before packaging. Expect a bright, clean cup with vibrant fruit notes, subtle floral undertones, and smooth natural sweetness.

Process: ing, where the skin and pulp are removed
Desc: After harvesting, ripe coffee cherries are brought to the factory by smallholder farmers for wet processing, where the skin and pulp are removed. This process relies on electrical pumps to bring water from the nearest source into reservoir tanks. To conserve water, the factory recirculates it during processing. A disc pulper with three sets of discs is used to separate the skin and fruit from the green coffee beans. Following pulping, the coffee ferments overnight to break down sugars, then it is cleaned, soaked, and spread on raised drying tables. The drying time varies based on climate conditions and the volume of coffee being processed.

Desc: After harvesting, ripe coffee cherries are brought to the factory by smallholder farmers for wet processing, where the skin and pulp are removed. This process relies on electrical pumps to bring water from the nearest source into reservoir tanks. To conserve water, the factory recirculates it during processing. A disc pulper with three sets of discs is used to separate the skin and fruit from the green coffee beans. Following pulping, the coffee ferments overnight to break down sugars, then it is cleaned, soaked, and spread on raised drying tables. The drying time varies based on climate conditions and the volume of coffee being processed.

Name: Melkodige Anaerobic
Desc: Ripe red cherries with a Brix content over 24% are handpicked and washed in a water bath. They are then surface dried and inoculated with Lalcafe saccharomyces yeast. The cherries are placed in airtight containers for 72 hours of anaerobic fermentation, during which the yeast converts sugars into enzymes, esters, and alcohol, creating a unique flavor. After fermentation, the cherries are dried slowly on raised wooden trays for over twenty days.

Name: Raxidi Naturals
Desc:
After selective picking of the best coffee cherries, the cherries were washed and kept in a stainless steel container. We used a strain called W1 which is a mix of yeast and bacteria to ferment the cherries for 48 hours in an anaerobic condition. After which they were removed and taken to raised beds for slow drying for 21 days. In the drying yard a controlled environment was maintained accounting for temperature and humidity which was monitored regularly. 
 Raxidi Estate, located at an elevation of 950-1000 meters in Sakleshpur, Karnataka, spans 165 acres and has been nurtured by three generations of the Lobo family since the 1950s. Currently, father-daughter duo Richard and Rachel Lobo continue this legacy, cultivating Arabica varieties such as Selection 6, Catimore, and Chandragiri, alongside Robusta varieties like old Peredenia and Selection 270. Their focus on micro-lots and innovative processing techniques results in coffee with unique depth and character, with every step, from handpicking cherries to using pure spring water, executed with precision.

Name: RC-7 Naturals
Tasting_Notes: This is a 60-hour anaerobic fermentation natural
Desc: This is a 60-hour anaerobic fermentation natural processed coffee. It is from the Hemavathi varietal grown on our farm at 4450 feet from the block called Sivermara Patte. The Brix of the coffee cherries was 24.6 when harvested and they were put in the fermenters after floater removal. A strain of lab culture microbes were them introduced in a Nitrogen rich environment and allowed to ferment for 60 hours at 2.2 bar pressure. After removing the coffee from the fermenters, it was directly put on raised beds and dried for 29 days.

Desc: The coffee cherries which are pulped using clean spring water, effectively removing the mucilage from the seeds. To ensure consistency and uniformity in every batch, the green beans are then immersed in clean water for 24 to 30 hours. After this soaking process, the beans are dried on raised beds for 25 to 30 days. Throughout the drying process, we meticulously inspect and remove any defective beans. The remaining good beans are slow-dried until they reach an optimal moisture level of 11%.

Name: Sandalkad Herb Fermented
Tasting_Notes: such as sugarcane and dried coconut
Desc: The cherries undergo a fermentation process lasting 72 hours in an anaerobic environment, where they are combined with wild herbs sourced from the farm. This method helps balance acidity and develop optimal flavor profiles. Following fermentation, the cherries are dried in the shade, which helps preserve their complex characteristics. The end product is a coffee known for its rich flavor and exceptional quality, featuring tasting notes such as sugarcane and dried coconut.

Name: The Lacto Project
Tasting_Notes: This coffee has undergone a 96-hour extended carbonic maceration
Desc: This coffee has undergone a 96-hour extended carbonic maceration. Processed naturally, made from the Hemavathi varietal, grown at 4500 feet in the SIVERMARA Patte block. The cherries had a Brix of 25.9 at harvest and were placed in Bio fermenters after floater removal. They were inoculated with various lab-grown cultures, purged with carbon dioxide, and fermented for 96 hours. After fermentation, the beans were dried slowly on raised beds for 31 days, with constant stirring.

Name: Thermal Shock
Desc: This particular lot goes through an exciting Thermal Shock Anaerobic Fermentation process in high-tech bio fermenters for 36 hours! This unique method really brings out the coffee's natural sweetness and clarity, making every sip a delightful tasting adventure. You'll get to enjoy a lovely tropical mix of flavors, including Pear, Green Apple Candy, and Blackberries. It's all about creating a fun and flavorful experience in your cup!

Name: Toffee Club
Tasting_Notes: This is a 48-hour LAB
Desc: This is a 48-hour LAB PROCESS washed coffee from the Hemavathi varietal, grown at 4325 feet in the SILVERMARA Patte block. With a Brix of 25.4 at harvest, the cherries underwent fermentation in Bio fermenters with added microbes and lactic acid bacteria for 48 hours in a CO2-rich environment. After de-pulping and washing, the coffee was slowly dried for 24 days on raised beds with constant stirring.

Name: Melkodige Estate Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals
Tasting_Notes: Watermelon, Stone Fruit like Plum & Vibrant Acidity ||
Desc:
Tastes Like  -   Pomegranate, Pink Guava and Golden Raisins 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals 
 
   Varietal -  Sl 9  
   Altitude -  1280 MASL    
   Producer Name     -  Aveen and Yogita Rodrigues   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -       R  ed, fully ripe cherries with a Brix level above 22 are selectively handpicked and carefully cleaned using a water bath to remove impurities and lighter fruit. The cherries then undergo anaerobic fermentation in sealed drums for 72 hours, allowing complex flavours to develop. 
 Post-fermentation, they are transferred to raised wooden drying beds and dried slowly under shade nets. During this stage, the cherries are regularly raked to ensure even and consistent drying. Once fully dried, they are packed into gunny bags and rested for 60 days, allowing the flavours to stabilise and mature before further processing. 
      Roasters Note  -      We’ve taken this coffee light to preserve its vibrancy and showcase the fruit character developed during fermentation. Expect a bright, expressive cup with juicy acidity and a clean, lingering sweetness. In the cup: Pomegranate leads with a fresh, winey brightness, followed by soft pink guava and a rounded golden raisin sweetness on the finish. The body is smooth and supple, with a crisp yet balanced aftertaste. Best enjoyed when brewed clean and slightly cooler to let the fruit open up gradually.

Name: Salawara Estate Bioreactor Naturals
Tasting_Notes: Spiced Mandarin Tea , Dried Apple and Cranberry
Desc:
Tastes Like  -   Spiced Mandarin Tea , Dried Apple and Cranberry  
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Naturals 
 
   Varietal -  SL 795  
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     This lot was fermented in our newly introduced bioreactor, a state-of-the-art fermentation system designed to ensure precise control and homogeneous fermentation. The coffees were placed in the bioreactor for 72 hours, where temperature, oxygen levels, and microbial activity were carefully managed. A specially selected yeast strain was introduced during fermentation to enhance and amplify the fruit-forward characteristics of the coffee. Once fermentation was complete, the coffee was removed from the bioreactor and dried slowly on raised beds, allowing the developed flavors to stabilize and fully express themselves in the final cup.  
      Roasters Note  -       This coffee is a beautiful example of controlled fermentation done right. Processed in a state-of-the-art bioreactor over 72 hours with carefully managed temperature, oxygen, and a selected yeast strain, the result is an exceptionally clean yet expressive cup. Roasted for filter to highlight clarity and sweetness, it opens up with a vibrant spiced mandarin tea character, followed by layers of dried apple and a crisp cranberry finish. Bright, fruit-forward, and structured , a lot that feels both lively and refined.

Name: Salawara Estate Carbonic Maceration
Tasting_Notes: Watermelon, Stone Fruit like Plum & Vibrant Acidity ||
Desc:
Tastes Like  -    Watermelon, Orange Blossom, and Damson Plum          
 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Carbonic Maceration Naturals  
 
   Varietal -   SL 795 + SL 6   
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     Ripe coffee cherries are carefully handpicked from  Dodda kere Patte, at a Brix level of 24. The cherries are then sealed in stainless steel tanks and pressurized with carbon dioxide for 72 hours, creating an anaerobic environment that initiates carbonic maceration. During this stage, intracellular fermentation occurs within the intact cherries, intensifying fruit-forward characteristics and enhancing aromatic complexity. After fermentation, the cherries are removed from the tanks and slowly dried on raised beds, preserving clarity, sweetness, and vibrant fruity flavors in the cup.  
      Roasters Note  -      We roasted this carbonic maceration lot with a focus on clarity and fruit expression. The profile brings out its watermelon-like juiciness and orange blossom aromatics, supported by a deeper damson plum sweetness. Development was kept controlled to retain acidity and structure while preserving a light, refreshing finish.

Name: Salawara Estate Mosto fermentation
Tasting_Notes: White peach, Golden Raisin and Bergamot
Desc:
Tastes Like  -   White peach, Golden Raisin and Bergamot 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Champagne Fermentation 
 
   Varietal -  SL 795  
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2024-2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     “Mosto” refers to the sweet, fermented juice extracted from coffee cherries or their mucilage, rich in natural sugars, acids, and a diverse microbial culture of yeasts and bacteria. Fresh coffee cherries are placed in large, food-grade barrels, and “musto” from a previous batch of natural coffees is added to accelerate fermentation and enhance complexity. The coffees are then slow-dried using a nursery-style drying method.  
      Roasters Note  -      In the cup, expect a delicate interplay of white peach and golden raisin, bringing a soft, rounded sweetness, while bergamot lifts the profile with a fragrant, citrusy brightness. The acidity is elegant with a silky mouthfeel and a clean, lingering finish. The nursery-style drying further refines the structure of the cup, preserving aromatics while enhancing sweetness and balance. A refined and aromatic profile. ideal for those who enjoy floral, fruit-forward coffees with a composed fermentation character.

Tasting_Notes: Green Apple, Prune and Creamy Mouthfeel
Desc:
Tastes Like  -   Green Apple, Prune and Creamy Mouthfeel  
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Honey Sun Dried 
 
   Varietal -  SL 6 + SL 9  
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2024-2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     The coffees were harvested from Block 24 at a Brix level of 22. This lot underwent yeast inoculation using Pichia and Lactobacillus, fermented in large stainless-steel tanks. Carbon dioxide was introduced during fermentation to enhance the coffee’s fruity flavour profile. The coffee was then processed using the natural method and slow-dried for 22 days in a controlled nursery drying system.  
      Roasters Note  -      This lot shows a bright green-apple acidity layered over prune-like sweetness. We roasted it to keep those fruit tones intact while allowing the creamy mouthfeel to carry through on the finish. Development was kept controlled to retain clarity and balance without compromising texture, making it suited for both filter and modern espresso styles.

Name: SCA Brewing Foundation Course

Origin: Corridor Seven Coffee Academy [ Map Link ]
Process: ing methods, and best practices for coffee storage
Desc:
The Brewing Foundation course offers a comprehensive introduction to the art and science of coffee brewing. Through both theory and hands-on practice, learners are guided through various brewing methods using a range of devices. 
 This course is ideal for beginners and provides the fundamental skills and knowledge needed to craft delicious brewed coffee.  
  Time:  10:30 AM - 6:30 PM 
  Location:  Corridor Seven Coffee Academy [ Map Link ] 
  What You'll Learn:    
  1. Coffee Knowledge :  Understand Arabica vs. Robusta, processing methods, and best practices for coffee storage. 
  2. Brewing Methods & Equipment :  Explore manual brewers like V60, French Press, and AeroPress, and learn how to use essential brewing tools. 
  3. Brewing Guidelines :  Master the 7 key elements of brewing: ratio, grind, time, temperature, turbulence, water quality, and filter type. 
  4. Brewing Techniques :  Practice percolation (V60), immersion (French Press), and hybrid (AeroPress) brewing styles. 
  5. Brew Analysis :  Learn to evaluate your brew by analyzing its color, aroma, taste, and body. 
  6. Equipment Maintenance :  Maintain your brewing tools for consistency, cleanliness, and long-term performance.

Name: ARABICA PEABERRY COFFEE
Tasting_Notes: At Devans, Arabica Peaberry is
Desc:
ANIMAL PRINTED PACKS AVAILABLE IN 500 g ONLY 
  Indian coffees are home to the best shade grown coffees in the world. It grows Arabica and Robusta coffees in the southern states where lush coffee plantations are heavily inter cropped with black pepper and ginger that bustle with honeybees and yield the finest coffee beans.  
  Peaberry coffees are rare, comprising only 3-7% of the total crop. These pea-shaped, natural formations of the coffee bean are thought to form when several pistils get knocked off the coffee flower, causing only one seed to form inside the coffee fruit rather than two.  
  Normally coffee beans grow two to a cherry, flat against each other but in about five percent of the worlds coffee a bean is found to be solo that's Peaberry.  
  Because there's no way to tell from looking at the cherry whether there's a single or double bean inside, as a result Peaberry beans are hand picked and processed to be enjoyed separately.  
 Tasting notes:    
  At Devans, Arabica Peaberry is roasted in a way to create a mild strength of coffee, that is soft, smooth, highly aromatic and flavorful . If you like milder coffees, go for this lighter bodied and a clean cup of coffee. It’s ideal when made in a French Press or a pour over.

Desc:

  Black Tea Spring Harvest- March-April 2025  
  Darjeeling First Flush tea especially roasted for DEVANS from Giddapahar tea estate.  
  Fresh Harvest - April    2025  
  Giddapahar tea garden is located on the Kurseong valley in Darjeeling. The tea bushes grow at an elevation from 4500 to 5200 feet from the sea level. This tea estate is known for its exquisite and characteristic Darjeeling teas grown from century old China bushes. Especially roasted for Devan’s - this is the First Pick of the year 2025.  
   Directly sourced from the Tea Garden in Darjeeling. Small lot, unique, especially roasted for Devans. 
  First Flush is defined as the very first picking of a tea plant’s harvest season. The new leaves plucked during First Flush are the youngest and most tender part of the tea plant and are said to yield the purest and freshest cup of tea. Each additional Flush produces a different flavour and aroma as the growing season for that tea plant progresses.  
  This first flush is of a superior grade and has undergone minimal oxidation which ensures the natural sweetness, freshness and flavours are retained, while giving the tea a mellow and smooth cup. There is a hint of floral fruitiness that reveals itself, with subtle notes of citrus around the edges. The lingering sweetness towards the end stays with you for quite some time.

Name: MONSOONED MALABAR - ARABICA AA
Tasting_Notes: Monsooned flavor, low on acidity, mellow taste and a golden color in the cup
Desc:
ANIMAL PRINTED PACKS AVAILABLE IN 500 g ONLY. 
  Monsooned Malabar AA pure arabica, is a specialty coffee of India and one of the world's most sought after Indian coffee beans. These exotic beans undergo a unique process, beans are cured only on the Malabar coast during the south-west monsoon months of June to September that results in producing their amazing flavor profile. Sun dried green beans are warehoused only on the Malabar coast, in the west coast of India, where deliberate exposure to the sea air and monsoon winds result in the beans to swell, fade and reduce acidity.  
  Tasting Notes  
  Monsooned flavor, low on acidity, mellow taste and a golden color in the cup. Medium roasted to bring out notes of spice, mustiness, wood, chocolate and nuts. It has a sweetish finish, adding very rich crema to espresso cup.

Name: ROOIBOS TEA
Desc:
Rooibos tea is made from the leaves of "red bush" plant, which grows only in the small Cederberg region of South Africa. Because it does not derive from the Camillia sinensis plant (like black, white, green or oolong teas), rooibos tea is considered more of an herbal drink or tisane than a "true" tea. Rooibos tea is often called "red tea" or "red bush" tea because of the bright red coloring the leaves take on during the oxidation and fermentation processes. A properly brewed cup of rooibos tea will be a rich red color and have a sweet, nutty flavour.

Name: Frozen Cherry Imperial - Jannapura Estate
Tasting_Notes: 🍒 Cherry-forward sweetness 🍵 Earl Grey tea elegance 🥤 Cola-like depth 🍎 Apple brightness 🍇 Dry berries & raisin
Desc:
Jannapura Estate – Frozen Cherry Imperial  
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
 Perched in the lush highlands of Chikmagalur, Jannapura Estate presents  Frozen Cherry Imperial —a bold and experimental nanolot that redefines fruit-forward coffee through precision processing and controlled fermentation. 
 This lot begins with carefully handpicked, fully ripened coffee cherries that are  frozen in an industrial freezer for 48 hours . This freezing step enhances cellular breakdown, allowing deeper infusion of flavours during the next stage. The cherries are then  anaerobically fermented with yeast , developing a complex and layered profile, before being  slowly dried on raised beds for 18 days  to lock in clarity and sweetness. 
 The result is a strikingly expressive cup—vivid, structured, and deeply aromatic. Expect a unique interplay of tea-like elegance and dark fruit intensity, with a profile that stands apart in both complexity and character. 
 📍  Jannapura Estate – Chikmagalur, Karnataka  🌿  Varietals:  Selection 795 | Elevation: 3600–3900 ft 🕒  48h Cryo (Frozen) + Anaerobic Fermentation  🌞  18 Days Raised Bed Drying  
 
  Tasting Notes:  
 🍒 Cherry-forward sweetness 🍵 Earl Grey tea elegance 🥤 Cola-like depth 🍎 Apple brightness 🍇 Dry berries & raisin richness 
 
 Experience the intensity of  Frozen Cherry Imperial , where controlled freezing meets fermentation to create a cup that is both innovative and unmistakably premium. 
  Resting Period = Minimum 10 days.

Name: KALYANCOOL MAHARANI
Tasting_Notes: 🌹 Rose Petals 🌼 Marigold 🎋 Sugarcane 🍯 Date Syrup 🍫 Cacao Nibs ✨ Spiced Finish 👑 The Cup Expect a refined and
Desc:
👑 Kalyancool Maharani 
 🌹  One of the most distinctive microlots produced at Kalyancool Estate this year.  
 Crafted through extended anaerobic fermentation, organic rose gulkand, and our proprietary Mélange Split Roast Technique, Maharani is an experimental microlot that explores a uniquely Indian expression of specialty coffee. 
 Built around patience rather than intensity, this lot delivers delicate florals, layered sweetness, and a refined spice-driven finish that unfolds gradually with every sip. 
 
 🌹 Rose Character Disclaimer 
 ⚠️  Please read before ordering  
 Maharani is not a traditional cultured coffee where microbial cultures are extracted directly from rose petals to create highly intense floral characteristics. 
 For this lot, we used standardized  Lalcafé Oro yeast  as the primary fermentation culture. Organic rose gulkand was introduced into the anaerobic fermentation environment to contribute additional floral complexity and aromatic compounds. 
 As a result, the rose character in the cup is elegant and integrated rather than overtly perfumed or dominant. 
 🌹  Rose Intensity: 2/5  
 Expect subtle rose petal aromatics that complement the coffee's natural sweetness and complexity rather than an intensely floral "rose-forward" cup. 
 
 ☕ Bean Appearance Disclaimer 
 ⚠️  Some beans may exhibit slight surface oils despite being roasted at a light roast level.  
 This is completely normal for this lot. 
 Only extremely ripe red cherries were selected for processing, followed by an extended  120-hour anaerobic fermentation . 
 The combination of high fruit maturity and prolonged fermentation may cause certain beans to develop a slight oily sheen even when roasted around first crack. 
 🔥 This is  not  a sign of darker roasting. 
 Customers are encouraged to judge quality by: 
 ✅ Aroma 
 ✅ Sweetness 
 ✅ Acidity 
 ✅ Cup Clarity 
 ✅ Overall Taste Experience 
 rather than bean appearance. 
 
 ☕ Roast Profile Available 
 🔥  Mélange Split Roast – Light Plus  
 🌱  100% Arabica  
 
 🔥 The Mélange Split Roast Technique 
 Maharani is roasted using our proprietary: 
 ✨  Mélange Split Roast Technique

 This roast profile helps preserve: 
 🌹 Floral aromatics

 ✨ Vibrant complexity 
 ☕  50% of the coffee is dropped at the end of First Crack  
 This roast profile contributes: 
 🍯 Sweetness

 🥮 Rounder mouthfeel 
 The two roast profiles are then blended in an exact  50:50 ratio . 
 The result is a layered cup that combines aromatics, sweetness, balance, and depth beyond what a single roast profile can achieve. 
 Because of this roast architecture, the beans may appear slightly uneven in colour. This is intentional and reflects the combination of two roast expressions rather than inconsistent roasting. 
 
 🌿 The Story Behind Maharani 
 Produced entirely at our own  Kalyancool Estate in Chikmagalur , Maharani began with carefully hand-selected fully ripened red cherries harvested at peak maturity. 
 Every batch was meticulously sorted, with all green cherries and floaters removed before processing. 
 The cherries then underwent our  Bruised Natural Process , where the fruit was gently beaten and bruised before fermentation. This intentional bruising partially opens many of the cherries while leaving others intact. 
 The objective is to create multiple fermentation environments within the same lot. The opened cherries allow deeper interaction between fruit sugars, yeast, and fermentation compounds, while the intact cherries preserve structure, clarity, and balance. 
 This combination produces a more layered and expressive cup than a conventional natural process. 
 The coffee was then transferred into an anaerobic environment and fermented for an extended  120 hours . 
 During fermentation, organic rose gulkand sourced from: 
 🌹 Two Brothers Organic Farms 
 🌹 Kapiva 
 was introduced alongside activated  Lalcafé Oro yeast 200g . 
 Approximately  5 kg of organic rose gulkand  was incorporated into the fermentation environment together with activated Oro yeast to contribute floral complexity, sweetness, and aromatic depth. 
 Following fermentation, the coffee was slowly dried on raised beds to preserve sweetness, clarity, and elegance.

Name: THERMAL SHOCK -  Ruby Pulse - Kalyancool Estate (In-House)
Tasting_Notes: 🍉 Watermelon 🍷 Grape Wine 🍎 Pomegranate 🍇 Dried Grapes 🍑 Prunes Experience Thermal Shock - Ruby Pulse —a striking
Desc:
Kalyancool Thermal Shock Fermentation – Ruby Pulse  
 This is one of the most technically experimental microlots we have produced this year—an expressive coffee that demonstrates how extreme temperature contrast and controlled fermentation can unlock deep fruit complexity and wine-like character. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
  100% Arabica  
 Rooted in our own estate at  Kalyancool , this microlot explores the effect of  thermal shock processing combined with controlled yeast fermentation . Carefully selected fully ripened red cherries are first sorted to remove floaters and underripe fruits, ensuring only dense, high-quality cherries enter the process. 
 The cherries are then subjected to a  thermal shock treatment , where they are immersed in  55°C warm water for 5 minutes . This controlled heat exposure helps soften the fruit structure and prepares the cherries for rapid cellular stress. Immediately after heating, the cherries are transferred to  ice chamber and rapidly chilled , remaining in the cold bath for around  7–8 minutes . 
 This dramatic temperature contrast creates a “thermal shock” effect that enhances permeability of the fruit and intensifies the interaction between sugars, microbes, and yeast during fermentation. 
 After the thermal treatment, the cherries are gently  bruised to create a bruised natural process , allowing partial opening of the fruit skin while maintaining the natural mucilage and pulp around the beans. 
 The cherries are then inoculated with  activated Lalcafe Intenso yeast , a strain chosen for its ability to enhance fruity aromatics and wine-like complexity. Fermentation takes place in  sealed Eco-tact bags for 72 hours , allowing controlled anaerobic conditions to develop layered fruit character. 
 Once fermentation is complete, the coffee is dried as naturals and carefully  light (light plus) roasted  to preserve clarity, acidity, and aromatic intensity. 
 The cup opens with  fresh watermelon sweetness , juicy and refreshing. This is followed by vibrant  pomegranate acidity , adding brightness and structure. As the coffee develops on the palate, deeper  grape-wine notes emerge , bringing a rich fermented fruit character. As the cup cools, darker fruit layers of  prunes and dried grapes  appear, creating a long, wine-like finish with lingering sweetness. 
 This is a bold experimental coffee designed to showcase how  thermal shock processing and precision fermentation can transform natural coffees into intensely fruit-driven microlots.  
 📍  Estate:  Kalyancool Estate, Chikmagalur 🌿  Process:  Thermal Shock Bruised Natural 🌡  Thermal Shock Step:  55°C warm water → immediate ice bath 🕒  Fermentation:  72 hours anaerobic fermentation 🌱  Yeast:  Lalcafe Intenso 🔥  Roast:  Light 
  Varietal:  Chandragiri, Selection 795 
 Tasting Notes 
 🍉 Watermelon 🍷 Grape Wine 🍎 Pomegranate 🍇 Dried Grapes 🍑 Prunes 
   
 Experience  Thermal Shock - Ruby Pulse  —a striking experimental microlot where extreme temperature contrast, bruised natural processing, and controlled fermentation combine to produce a vibrant, wine-like cup. 
  Resting Period:  Minimum 10 days.

Process: Natural Process with Whisky Barrel Aging
Desc:
Udaygiri Estate Whisky Barrel Aged – Oak Reserve  
 This is one of the most refined barrel-aged coffees we have roasted this year—an elegant microlot where specialty coffee meets the depth and character of whisky oak maturation. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
  100% Arabica  
 Sourced from  Udaygiri Estate in Chikmagalur , this microlot explores how oak maturation can enhance coffee complexity while preserving clarity and fruit structure. 
 Carefully selected ripe cherries are processed as naturals and dried to the ideal moisture level. Once stabilized, the green beans are transferred into  seasoned whisky barrels  that previously held aged whisky. The beans are then  rested inside the barrels for several weeks , allowing the porous green coffee to slowly absorb the aromatic compounds embedded in the oak. 
 During this maturation period, the beans take on subtle layers of  oak wood tannins, vanilla sweetness, and whisky-like aromatic complexity , while still preserving the natural fruit character of the coffee. 
 Once the desired infusion is achieved, the beans are removed and roasted  Light Plus , ensuring the barrel characteristics remain elegant and integrated rather than overpowering. 
 The cup opens with crisp  green apple acidity , bright and refreshing. This is followed by juicy layers of  kiwi, grapes, and stone fruits , adding a lively fruit sweetness that balances the barrel influence. As the coffee develops, the profile deepens into rich  whisky-like warmth , supported by pronounced  oakwood structure  and delicate  vanilla undertones  that linger into the finish. 
 This is a sophisticated coffee that highlights how  barrel aging can complement specialty coffee without overshadowing its natural fruit profile.

Tasting_Notes: 🍈 Musk Melon 🍇 Raisin 🍪 Butter Cookie 🌰
Process: De-Pulped • Lalcafé Cima Yeast • 72-Hour Lactic Fermentation • Hand Washed
Desc:
Washed Gold – 72-Hour Lactic Washed 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
  Please Note:  This is a clean lactic-washed coffee and not a fruit-forward anaerobic natural. While controlled fermentation contributes complexity and sweetness, the cup remains elegant, structured, and clean. Customers seeking intense wine-like, boozy, or heavily fermented fruit characteristics may prefer our anaerobic natural offerings instead. This lot was intentionally processed to highlight the clarity, sweetness, balance, and nuanced character that premium washed coffees can offer when fermentation is used as a tool to enhance quality rather than dominate the cup.  Crafted for coffee drinkers who value clarity, balance, and sweetness rather than intense fruit-forward or funky fermentation characteristics.  
 Washed Gold is a refined lactic-washed microlot produced at Navees Farm by  Nirikshith A N , a modern coffee producer balancing a corporate career with a passion for farming and continuous innovation. With a strong focus on farm automation and quality-driven processing, this lot showcases how thoughtful fermentation can enhance sweetness and complexity while maintaining a clean cup. 
 The cherries are de-pulped and inoculated with  Lalcafé Cima yeast , followed by approximately  72 hours of controlled lactic fermentation . The coffee is then hand-washed to halt fermentation at the desired stage, resulting in a cup that is expressive yet remarkably clean. 
 Grown at elevations above  4,000 feet ASL , this coffee opens with the sweet, refreshing character of musk melon. As the cup develops, gentle raisin-like fruit notes emerge, supported by the comforting sweetness of butter cookies. Roasted almond adds structure and depth, while a smooth cocoa finish lingers pleasantly, creating a balanced and elegant drinking experience. 
 📍  Navees Farm  🌿  Produced by:  Nirikshith A N 🌿  Varietal:  Selection 795 |  Elevation:  4,000+ ft ASL 🔒  Process:  De-Pulped • Lalcafé Cima Yeast • 72-Hour Lactic Fermentation • Hand Washed 
  Tasting Notes:  🍈 Musk Melon 🍇 Raisin 🍪 Butter Cookie 🌰 Roasted Almond 🍫 Cocoa

The profile was kept deliberately short, finishing at an  ultra-light endpoint with 15-16% development , just enough to stabilise the structure without muting the fruit.Anaerobic coffees can easily tip into heavy, ferment-driven profiles. Desc:
#1 SERIES - FRUIT FORWARD LOTS | Cane & Lime  
 
   Dense & Sugar-driven flavours in your final cup.

  Based on Sensory Evaluation  
 
   Sweet lime & gooseberry brightness, layered over dense sugar-driven base of jaggery & sugarcane

    Light-Medium Roast  with high air flow & 14-15 % development.  
 
 
 
  Characteristics  
 
   Juicy mouthfeel with a medium body & bright, clean acidity.   
 
 
 
  Minimum resting period  
   Filter 7 Days | Espresso 14 Days

  About the region / estate :   
 At a maximum elevation of 5300 feet above MSL, the coffees from the Yelnoorkhan Estate are in a class of their own. These high elevation coffees are much sought-after and have the rare distinction of having been sold under the Yelnoor Khan Mist brand name in North America in the early 2000s. 
 Established in the early 1900s, this estate was taken over by Kelachandra Coffee in 2021. Located in the direct vicinity of the Mullayanagiri peak, it tells the story of the history and origins of coffee culture in India. Due to the terrain’s harsh demands, handpicked coffee continues to remain a uniquely Indian tradition, even as the rest of the world moves on to mechanization. The ethos of respect for the land and the crop directly translates into one of Kelachandra Coffee’s finest single-origin produce.  
  Roasters thought :  
 High elevation coffees tend to carry tighter cell structure and higher organic acid content. To manage this, we used  high airflow throughout the roast , allowing for cleaner heat transfer and avoiding any roast-induced heaviness that could mask the cup’s definition. 
 The profile was taken to a  light–medium endpoint with ~14% development , giving just enough time to round off sharper acids while maintaining the coffee’s natural brightness and juiciness. 
 Rather than extending development, we prioritised a  clean and efficient Maillard phase , ensuring that sweetness builds without muting the acidity. 
 In the cup, this translates to a  structured citrus profile , where  sweet lime and gooseberry  define the front, supported by a dense,  sugarcane and jaggery-driven sweetness .   
 
  Brew Approach:  
 18.5 GMS Med-Fine (Fellow Ode Gen 2.0, 3.9 Setting) 55 ML bloom 45 seconds  Swirl immediately after pour Then 80 ML Then At 1.30 again 80 ML Then again 95 ML to finish it off with gentle swirl in the end.  
 Water at 94  °  Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).    
 For  more brightness (lime forward)  → go slightly coarser + reduce final pour agitation 
 For  more sweetness (jaggery heavy)  → grind finer + extend brew closer to 2:50

  A song that pairs well  
    
 
 
 
   
  Roaster thoughts :   After Mango in Loop we as roasters are creating a similar and complex blend of arabica called Strawberry in Loop. This blend releases an aroma of red ripe berries immediately post grinding it. It can be enjoyed both with and without milk especially a cortado. As roasters the creation of this blend took us over 3 months, after several roasting profiles & blending lots different ways to eventually do over a dozen espresso trials. Expect an  invigorating aroma, sweet rich espresso and a final cup full of red berry sweetness.  
   Brew Approach :   
 18.5 Gram -> 45 ML (1:2.25) Temperature 93-95 C Extraction time 25 sec Steady pressure of 9 
 Pressure profiling, Start: 2 bars → 6 bars at 10 sec → hold at 9 bars from 10–30 sec 
  Brew Better: Water & Resting Guidelines  
 Water is just as important as the beans. For the cleanest, most balanced cup, we recommend using **mineral water with a Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) level not above 140 ppm**. This will allow the true flavor of your coffee to shine. 
 Rested Coffee = Better Coffee 
 Freshly roasted coffee continues to evolve. Harsh or roasty notes fade, giving way to sweetness, clarity, and complexity. 
 Our resting guide: 
 Minimum rest (Filter): 10 days after roast date Minimum rest (Espresso): Up to 3 weeks after roast date 
 Patience pays off. Let your coffee settle, and enjoy a cup that truly reflects its origin.

Desc:

Name: Golden Hour
Tasting_Notes: that one rare moment you actually pause - mid-scroll, mid-chaos - when the sunlight spills in and for no reason at all
Desc:
Like a soft spotlight through the blinds - orange zest, stone fruit, and juicy apple line up for their solo. It's plum, but polished. This cup? It tastes like that one rare moment you actually pause - mid-scroll, mid-chaos - when the sunlight spills in and for no reason at all, you smile. Just for existing. It’s your reminder: reset the clock.  
  ROAST LEVEL:  Medium Light 
   PROCESSING:  Washed 
  REGION:  Hoyasala Estate (  Tamil Nadu ) &  The Laks Farm(Tamil Nadu) 
  ALTITUDE:  1300 MASL (metres above sea level) 
  VARIETAL:  SL9 
  HARVEST:  2025 
  BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual (French Press, Aeropress, Pour-over, Channi style, South Indian Filter) 
  BEVERAGE STYLE:  Manual Brew, Milk Based Drinks  
  Where Golden Hour Grows  Golden Hour is born where stillness meets intention - on two farms that honour the land, the craft, and the quiet magic of doing things the right way. 
 In the Pulney Hills of Tamil Nadu, you’ll find The Laks Farm in Pachalur village. One of the highest coffee-growing regions in India, it's a place where biodiversity thrives, coffee trees growing alongside oranges, bananas, cardamom, and pepper. Everything here is organic, intentional, and deeply alive. The result? Coffees that are bright, layered, and lingering like light catching the edge of the day. 
 Down south in Anoor village, Hoysala Estate carries the weight of history, named after a dynasty that once ruled this very soil. The estate has been family-run since the late 1800s, with a quiet focus on growing coffee that speaks for itself. At 1100 meters, intercropped with cardamom and processed with care - natural, washed, honey, and even monsooned, their approach is steady, patient, and precise. 
 Together, these two farms create something balanced and beautiful. Golden Hour is a blend full of grace and is soft, rounded, and golden in every sense.

Desc:

Name: Raincheck
Tasting_Notes: Citrus and sweet lime sneak in like a memory
Desc:
Heavy-bodied and emotionally available. Caramel wraps you like an old jumper. Citrus and sweet lime sneak in like a memory. And that chocolate? It lingers like a song you didn’t know you missed. This one doesn't just brew - it   drips  . You’ll want to cancel your plans and call it nostalgia.  
   
   ROAST LEVEL:  Medium Plus    
   PROCESSING:  Washed + Naturals&nbsp;  
   REGION:   Venkids Valley Estate(Karnataka) &  Harley Estate(Karnataka)  
   ALTITUDE:  1200 MASL (metres above sea level)    
   VARIETAL:  SLN 9 + SLN 795     
   HARVEST:  2025    
   BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual (Espresso, Moka Pot, South Indian Filter, Aeropress, French Press)    
   BEVERAGE STYLE:  Cold Brew, Manual Brews, Milk Based Drinks  
   
  Where Raincheck Grows  
    Raincheck   is grown where rain isn't a disruption, it's a rhythm. Two estates, two approaches, one shared respect for water, weather, and waiting for the right moment.  
  At   Venkids Valley Estate  , in the lush hills near Madikeri, nature sets the pace. This 200-acre expanse hums with wild fig, mango, avocado, and soapnut trees. Birds nest, breezes carry song, and coffee grows slowly beneath a dense canopy at 3600 feet. Pavan and Shilpa run the estate with quiet conviction, solar-powered homes, rainwater harvesting, and a community that’s been part of the land for decades. Here, modern machinery meets old-school care, and every bean reflects the patience of a place that listens to the rain.  
  Then there’s   Harley Estate  , further south in Sakleshpur. One of Karnataka’s most storied coffee farms, it balances heritage with innovation. With misty mornings and rich soil, Harley produces washed and natural coffees, and is known for its pioneering work in monsoon processing. Water isn’t just weather here, it’s part of the profile. Beans are aged in precisely controlled conditions, echoing the old shipping-route serendipity of monsooned coffee, but crafted with intention.  
  Together, these estates deliver a cup that’s moody, mellow, and quietly complex.   Raincheck   is for slow sippers and everything worth waiting for.

Name: Troublemaker
Tasting_Notes: Apricot and dark caramel pull you in, but it’s that figgy depth and nutty thump that makes you stay
Desc:
This one? It doesn't ask for permission. Think sweet lime with a side of defiance. Apricot and dark caramel pull you in, but it’s that figgy depth and nutty thump that makes you stay. With milk or straight-up bold - it doesn’t care. It’s for the ones who rewrite the rules while sipping their second cup.  
  ROAST LEVEL : Medium 
   PROCESSING:  Washed + Naturals 
  REGION:   Venkids Valley Estate (Karnataka) &  The Laks Farm (Tamil Nadu) 
  ALTITUDE:  1300 MASL (metres above sea level) 
  VARIETAL:  Chandragiri + SLN 9 + Canephora 
  HARVEST:  2025 
  BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual (French Press, Aeropress, Pour-over, South Indian Filter, Cold Brew) 
  BEVERAGE STYLE:  Cold Brew, Manual Brew, Milk Based Drinks  
  Where The Trouble Brews  
 Troublemaker isn’t born in one place. It comes from two farms, two philosophies, and one shared spirit: do things differently, and do them with intent. 
 First, there’s Venkids Valley Estate, tucked away in the Western Ghats near Madikeri. A winding road leads you in, past rivulets and wild fig trees, into 200 acres of untamed green. Pavan and Shilpa run the show, welcoming, passionate, and quietly rebellious. Here, at 3600 feet, coffee grows under a dense jungle canopy alongside over 40 species of trees. It’s processed with precision, but powered by people, a close-knit team living in solar-powered homes, harvesting rainwater, and keeping the land alive with every step. 
 Then, high in the Pulney Hills of Tamil Nadu, there’s The Laks Farm, nestled in Pachalur village. One of the highest coffee-growing regions in India, it runs on organic principles and deep respect for the ecosystem. No chemicals. No shortcuts. Just a farm where coffee grows with oranges, bananas, cardamom, and pepper, layered in flavor and full of life. 
 Together, these farms bring you a coffee that’s bold, bright, and a little wild. Just like its name. Troublemaker doesn’t play safe. It plays real.

Name: Banana Kents by Balanoor Plantation
Process: PSD Cup Notes – Jaggery Bites, Plum, Cocoa
Desc: Location – Chikmagalur, Karnataka    Altitude – 1200 Masl    Varietal – Kents    Process – PSD    Cup Notes – Jaggery Bites, Plum, Cocoa    Roast Profile – Medium   Net wt. - 250 g | 8.8 oz   Merthi Subbangudigy Estate (MS Estate) is located in the Sahyadari ranges of the Western Ghats, Chikmagalur, Karnataka. The estate is part of Balanoor Plantations which is run by Mr Ashok Kuriyan and his son Mr Rohan Kuriyan. Arabicas (rain forest certified) are grown under the shade of tress like, Silver Oaks, Dadaps and various jungle woods. Special attention is paid to every aspect of picking, pulping, fermenting, washing, drying and curing. The practice of sustainability and environmental responsibility is the heart of the farm.   About the Process-   The Kents banana leaf psd is a special coffee for us as it's one of the first experiments we did last year which succeeded. The coffee is carefully harvested to ensure only the best cherry is taken for this nano lot. The cherries are pulped trying to retain as much mucilage on the bean before it is dried on the raised beds under fresh banana leaves. The coffee is raked frequently and the leaves changed when it dries. The pulp and the banana leaf give these coffees it's sweet cupping notes.

  Our Latest Barrel-Aged Coffees are an experimental lot of specialty coffee beans from the highest peaks of Chikmagalur aged to perfection in the finest French Wine Cask Barrels. The resultant coffee is a cup that has a heady aroma complementing the sweet nuances of fine malt and grapes. We recommend a paper-based Aeropress or Pour Over brew method to really bring out the crisp inherent notes of this treasure!  
   Barrel-aged coffee is the process of rolling coffee beans in an aged barrel once used for aging wine or whiskey. This rolling process allows the beans to soak in the flavor and aromas of the barrel. The coffee beans are then roasted. This process gives the coffee flavour notes soaked up from the barrels

Name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe Grade 1 Idido
Tasting_Notes: Jasmine, Bergamot, Lemon Zest, Stone Fruit, Cane Sugar, Tea-like Body & Clean Finish
Desc:
Yirgacheffe Grade 1 Idido Ethiopian Specialty Arabica Coffee Beans 250g  
 
 
   
  Ethiopian Yirgacheffe Grade   1 – Idido  is a floral masterpiece. Grown at high elevations in the Gedeo Zone and washed for clarity, this coffee delivers delicate jasmine, bergamot, and lemon zest notes with a silky tea-like body and crisp acidity. Best brewed as a pour-over or Chemex, it's a favorite for black coffee lovers seeking refined and elegant cups. 
 
 
  Region:   Yirgacheffe, Gedeo Zone, Ethiopia 
 
 
  Elevation:   ~ 1,900–2,100 masl 
 
 
  Processing:   Washed (Grade 1) 
 
 
  Varietals:   Heirloom Ethiopian landraces 
 
 
   Roast Recommendation :  Light to Light-Medium 
 
 
  Cup Style: Delicate, floral, and tea-like  – a clean, elegant cup with bright citrus-laced acidity, silky mouthfeel, and lingering floral aftertaste. This is a quintessential washed Ethiopian profile:  refined, layered, and complex , ideal for slow sips and aroma appreciation.

Desc:
Gaggia Anima Class 
 
 
  The Soul of Espresso with Gaggia adapting system to always have the right amount of ground coffee for your espresso  
  The best in class one-touch cappuccino coffee machines. Designed and manufactured in Italy. Offers cappuccino, espresso, long black coffee, and latte macchiato at the click of a button. This is an excellent coffee machine for the office with a staff strength of 10. The machine has a capacity to brew 30-40 cups of coffee per day. It has a double-walled milk carafe that can be refrigerated when the machine is not in use and reattached when required. It’s the most effective coffee machine in the one-touch cappuccino product category. The optiaroma has 5 options of strength from 6.5 grams to 11 grams. you can thus select the strength of the beverage you like. Features:  
  1. Integrated milk Carafe  
  2. Premium Materials used  
  3. Automatic milk Frother  
  4. Removable water container.  
  The integrated milk carafe froths milk for an incredibly dense, consistent, and hot coffee, thanks to its unique two frothing chambers. It delivers a splash-free stream of velvety milk straight into your cup. The Anima class is equipped with a robust ceramic coffee grinder that turns beans into a fine powder and extracts maximum flavors, without ever tasting burnt. It has 5 different settings for the grind that offer a fine grind for a full-bodied espresso or a coarser grind for a light-tasting coffee.  
 The Gaggia Anima Class is similar to the Anima Prestige model in the Anima range of automatic espresso machines. the difference is in the body. The Anima Class has a Silver/Grey easy to clean plastic body. The Class model incorporates a milk carafe. The Anima Class is an ideal machine for luxurious, convenient cappuccino every time. 
 The Anima Class also offers precise control over the dosage of coffee beans per espresso shot, ranging from 7 to 11.5 grams. As well as this, the temperature of the beverages can also be controlled through the digital interface.

Gaggia Classic EVO Colour Vibes 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  Unleash your innner barista at Home  
  Get ready for the ultimate barista experience at home. With a professional chromed brass group and filter holder to ensure a perfect Italian espresso at home. Backed with a new intuitive user interface, a professional steam wand and new body shape that makes the water level visible.  
 The new Gaggia Classic is the culmination of our 80 years of tradition, history, and experience. We know that quality espresso is a ritual requiring the utmost care and attention so we built the best machine for the job. The traditional group, large solenoid valve and traditional filter holder ensure total control over the coffee; while the professional steam arm will froth the perfect microfoam for your cappuccinos. Stylishly designed and totally made in Italy. 
   
  Brand: Gaggia  
  Usage Type: Home & Offices    
 
 PROFESSIONAL STAINLESS STEEL FILTER-HOLDER  Designed to professional standards, the group head and filter holder are made of Stainless Steel to give you the best in espresso quality and machine longevity. SOLENOID VALVE  The three-way solenoid valve relieves the pressure in the filter holder immediately after pulling a shot. Water empties from the filter holder via the open valve, and into the drip tray. This leaves the coffee puck dry, making it easy to clean.   TRADITIONAL GAGGIA BOILER  Polished Aluminium boiler is designed for unparalleled temperature stability, giving you the best espresso every time you brew. The 15 bar pump pushes the hot water through the ground coffee at high pressure to ensure better tasting, crema topped, espresso. 
 
  PROFESSIONAL STEAM WAND WITH 2 STEAM OUTLETS  The perfect way to steam the milk, and make exquisitely silky, bar-quality microfoam.

CUP HOLDER   Espresso cups and glasses can be stored on the top of the machine for convenience, and to be ambiently heated by the boiler. A warm cup ensures that you espresso remains at the perfect temperature.    PROUDLY MADE IN ITALY   Guaranteed to be of premium quality, built with 80 years of passion for espresso making.

Tasting_Notes: Jaggery, Dark Chocolate, Honey, Citrus Finish | Body: Medium - Heavy
